sa_devanagari: विद्यापि चतुर्विधा | प्रत्यक्षलैङ्गिकस्मृत्यार्षलक्षणा ॥ ९८ ॥
sa_iast: vidyāpi caturvidhā | pratyakṣalaiṅgikasmṛtyārṣalakṣaṇā || 98 ||
literal_en: Vidyā also is of four kinds: (1) Directly sensuous, (2) Inferential, (3) Recollective and (4) Superhuman.—(III-i-8; IX-ii-1, 6, 23).

ml_draft.text: ഇനി വിദ്യ (പ്രമാത്മകജ്ഞാനം) നിരൂപിക്കപ്പെടുന്നു. വിദ്യയും നാലു വിധം — (1) പ്രത്യക്ഷം (ഇന്ദ്രിയങ്ങളിൽ നിന്ന് ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്നത്), (2) ലൈംഗികം (ലിംഗത്തിൽ നിന്ന് ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്നത് — അനുമാനം), (3) സ്മൃതി (ഓർമ), (4) ആർഷം (ഋഷിമാർക്കു മാത്രം ലഭ്യമായ അതീന്ദ്രിയജ്ഞാനം). ഇത് ഈ ലക്ഷണത്തോടു കൂടിയതാണ്.

en_simple_draft.text: Now *vidyā* (right cognition) is taken up. *Vidyā* too is fourfold: (1) *pratyakṣa* — directly sensuous, arising from the sense-organs; (2) *laiṅgika* — inferential, arising from the perception of an indicative mark (*liṅga*); (3) *smṛti* — recollective; and (4) *ārṣa* — the supersensuous intuition belonging to the *ṛṣi*s.

sa_devanagari: तत्राक्षम् अक्षम् प्रतीत्योत्पद्यते प्रतक्षम् | अक्षाणीन्द्रियाणि घ्राणरसनचक्षुस्त्वक्छ्रोत्रमनांसि षट् | तद् धि द्रव्यादिषु पदार्थेषूत्पद्यते | द्रव्ये तावद् द्विविधे महत्यनेकद्रव्यवत्त्वोद्भूतरूपप्रकाशचतुष्टयसन्निकर्षाद् धर्मादिसामग्र्ये च स्वरूपालोचनमात्रम् | सामान्यविशेषद्रव्यगुणकर्मविशेषणापेक्षाद् आत्ममनः सन्निकर्षात् प्रत्यक्षम् उत्पद्यते सद् द्रव्यम् पृथिवी विषाणी शुक्लो गौर्गच्छतीति | रूपरसगन्धस्पर्शेष्वनेकद्रव्यसमवायात् स्वगतविशेषात् स्वाश्रयसन्निकर्षान् नियतेन्द्रियनिमित्तम् उत्पद्यते | तेनैवोपलब्धिः | संख्यापरिमाणपृथक्त्वसम्योगविभागपरत्वापरत्वस्नेहद्रवत्ववेगकर्मणाम् प्रत्यक्षद्रव्यसमवायाच्चक्षुः स्पर्शनाभ्याम् ग्रहणम्  | बुद्धिसुखदुह्खेच्छाद्वेषप्रयत्नानाम् द्वयोरात्ममनसोः सम्योगाद् उपलब्धिः | भावद्रव्यत्वगुणत्वकर्मत्वादीनाम् उपलभ्याधारसमवेतानाम् आश्रयग्राहकैरिन्द्रियैर्ग्रहणम् इत्येतद् अस्मदादीनाम् प्रत्यक्षम्  | अस्मद्विशिष्टानाम् तु योगिनाम् युक्तानाम् योगजधर्मानुगृहीतेन मनसा स्वात्मान्तराकाशदिक्कालपरमणुवायुमनसस्सु तत्समवेतगुणकर्मसामान्यविशेषेषु समवाये चावितथम् स्वरूपदर्शनम् उत्पद्यते  | वियुक्तानाम् पुनश्चतुष्टयसन्निकर्षाद् योगजधर्मानुग्रहसामर्थयात् सूक्ष्मव्यवहितविप्रकृष्टेषु प्रत्यक्षम् उत्पद्यते | तत्र सामान्यविशेषेषु स्वरूपालोचनमात्रम् प्रत्यक्षम् प्रमाणम् प्रमेया द्रव्यादयः पदार्थाः प्रमानात्मा प्रमितिर्द्रव्यादिविषयम् ज्ञानम् | सामान्यविशेषज्ञानोत्पत्तावविभक्तम् आलोचनमात्रम् प्रत्यक्षम् प्रमाणम् अस्मिन् नान्यत्प्रमाणान्तरम् अस्ति अफलरूपत्वात् | अथवा सर्वेषु पदार्थेषु चतुष्टयसन्निकर्षाद् अवितथम् अव्यपदेश्यम् यज्ज्ञानम् उत्पद्यते तत्प्रत्यक्षम् प्रमाणम् प्रमेया द्रव्यादयः पदार्थाः प्रमातात्मा प्रमितिर्गुणदोषमाध्यस्थ्यदर्शनम् इति ॥ ९९ ॥
sa_iast: tatrākṣam akṣam pratītyotpadyate pratakṣam | akṣāṇīndriyāṇi ghrāṇarasanacakṣustvakchrotramanāṃsi ṣaṭ | tad dhi dravyādiṣu padārtheṣūtpadyate | dravye tāvad dvividhe mahatyanekadravyavattvodbhūtarūpaprakāśacatuṣṭayasannikarṣād dharmādisāmagrye ca svarūpālocanamātram | sāmānyaviśeṣadravyaguṇakarmaviśeṣaṇāpekṣād ātmamanaḥ sannikarṣāt pratyakṣam utpadyate sad dravyam pṛthivī viṣāṇī śuklo gaurgacchatīti | rūparasagandhasparśeṣvanekadravyasamavāyāt svagataviśeṣāt svāśrayasannikarṣān niyatendriyanimittam utpadyate | tenaivopalabdhiḥ | saṃkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvasamyogavibhāgaparatvāparatvasnehadravatvavegakarmaṇām pratyakṣadravyasamavāyāccakṣuḥ sparśanābhyām grahaṇam | buddhisukhaduhkhecchādveṣaprayatnānām dvayorātmamanasoḥ samyogād upalabdhiḥ | bhāvadravyatvaguṇatvakarmatvādīnām upalabhyādhārasamavetānām āśrayagrāhakairindriyairgrahaṇam ityetad asmadādīnām pratyakṣam | asmadviśiṣṭānām tu yoginām yuktānām yogajadharmānugṛhītena manasā svātmāntarākāśadikkālaparamaṇuvāyumanasassu tatsamavetaguṇakarmasāmānyaviśeṣeṣu samavāye cāvitatham svarūpadarśanam utpadyate | viyuktānām punaścatuṣṭayasannikarṣād yogajadharmānugrahasāmarthayāt sūkṣmavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭeṣu pratyakṣam utpadyate | tatra sāmānyaviśeṣeṣu svarūpālocanamātram pratyakṣam pramāṇam prameyā dravyādayaḥ padārthāḥ pramānātmā pramitirdravyādiviṣayam jñānam | sāmānyaviśeṣajñānotpattāvavibhaktam ālocanamātram pratyakṣam pramāṇam asmin nānyatpramāṇāntaram asti aphalarūpatvāt | athavā sarveṣu padārtheṣu catuṣṭayasannikarṣād avitatham avyapadeśyam yajjñānam utpadyate tatpratyakṣam pramāṇam prameyā dravyādayaḥ padārthāḥ pramātātmā pramitirguṇadoṣamādhyasthyadarśanam iti || 99 ||
literal_en:
Of these, that which proceeds from the senseorgans is ‘directly sensuous.’ The sense-organs are six—the nose, the tongue, the eye, the skin, the ear and the mind.

This knowledge appears with regard to substance and the other categories. As regards substance, it appears with reference to three forms of it, in the gross form; and proceeds from such causes as the existence of many parts, the appearance of manifested colour, and the presence of the contact of four things, aided by such auxiliaries as dharma and the like; in this the knowledge is in the character of ‘mere perception of form.’ From the contact of the mind as qualified by (1) generalities, (2) specialities, (3) substances, (4) qualities and (5) action,—there proceeds a ‘directly sensuous’ knowledge,—f.i., in the form, ‘the (1) existing, (2) substance, (3) earthy cow, (4) white and with horns, (5) is moving.’

With regard to colour, taste, odour, and touch the sensuous knowledge is brought about by means particular sense-organs, and proceeds from such causes as—their inherence in composite substances, peculiarities in the qualities themselves and the contact with the substrates of these qualities. The knowledge of sound proceeds from threefold contact; and inhering in the ear, it is known by the ear alone. Number, Dimension, Separateness, Conjunction, Disjunction, Distance, Proximity, Viscidity, Fluidity, Velocity and Action are perceived by the eye and the skin, through their inherence in perceptible substances. Intellect, Pleasure, Vain, Desire, Aversion and Effort are perceived by the contact of both mind and self. Bhāvatva (the character of ‘being’), guṇatva (the character ‘quality’) karma (the character of ‘action’) and others—when inhering in cognisable substrates—are perceived by means of those sense-organs that perceive their substrates. This is the case with our ordinary ‘sensuous’ knowledge.

As for persons unlike ourselves—e.g. yogis in the estatic condition—there appear precisely true cognitions of the real forms of such things as their awn self as well as the selves of ākāśa, space, time, atoms, wind, mind,—the qualities, actions, generalities and individualities inhering in these,—and inherence; and the cognition of these is brought about by the mind as aided; by properties or faculties born of yoga. In the case of Yogis out of the ecstastic coṇḍition, direct sensuous knowledge appears with regard io subtile, hidden and distant objects, by means of the mind through fourfold contact, by the force of faculties born of Yoga.

With regard io generalities and individualities, the only means of- direct sensuous knowledge is the perception or cognition of the mere form; the cognisable are substance and other categories; the cogniser is the self; and the cognition is the knowledge of substance, etc.

In the appearance of the cognition of generalities and individualities, the means of direct sensuous cognition consists in mere ‘ālocana’ (contact of the sense-organ and the object); for this there is no other means of knowledge; as it is not in the form of resultant cognition.

Or, the means of direct sensuous cognition may be defined as any and every true and undefinable cognition of all objects, following from fourfold contact; substance and other categories are the cognisables: the self is the cogniser; and the recognition of the good pleasant), bad (unpleasant) and indifferent character (of the things perceived) is the cognition.

ml_draft.text: ഇവയിൽ, അക്ഷങ്ങളെ (ഇന്ദ്രിയങ്ങളെ) ആശ്രയിച്ച് ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്ന ജ്ഞാനമാണു പ്രത്യക്ഷം. അക്ഷങ്ങൾ — അതായത് ഇന്ദ്രിയങ്ങൾ — ആറ്: ഘ്രാണം (മൂക്ക്), രസന (നാവ്), ചക്ഷുസ്സ് (കണ്ണ്), ത്വക്ക് (തൊലി), ശ്രോത്രം (ചെവി), മനസ്സ്. ഈ ജ്ഞാനം ദ്രവ്യാദി പദാർത്ഥങ്ങളെ കുറിച്ച് ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്നു. ദ്രവ്യത്തെ കുറിച്ച് — അനേകം അവയവങ്ങൾ ചേർന്ന സ്ഥൂലരൂപത്തിൽ — ഉദ്ഭൂതരൂപപ്രകാശം, ചതുഷ്ടയസന്നികർഷം (നാലിന്റെ സംയോഗം: ആത്മാ-മനസ്സ്-ഇന്ദ്രിയം-വിഷയം), ധർമ്മാദിസാമഗ്രി എന്നീ കാരണങ്ങളിൽ നിന്ന് സ്വരൂപാലോചനമാത്രം എന്ന വിധത്തിൽ ജ്ഞാനം ഉണ്ടാകുന്നു. സാമാന്യം, വിശേഷം, ദ്രവ്യം, ഗുണം, കർമ്മം എന്നിവയാൽ വിശേഷിക്കപ്പെട്ട മനസ്സിന്റെ ആത്മാവുമായുള്ള സന്നികർഷത്തിൽ നിന്ന് — 'സത്തുള്ള ദ്രവ്യമായ പൃഥിവിയിലെ കൊമ്പുള്ള വെളുത്ത പശു നടക്കുന്നു' എന്നതുപോലെ — പ്രത്യക്ഷജ്ഞാനം ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്നു. രൂപം, രസം, ഗന്ധം, സ്പർശം — ഇവയിൽ, അനേകദ്രവ്യങ്ങളിലെ സമവായം, സ്വന്തമായ വിശേഷം, സ്വാശ്രയസന്നികർഷം എന്നിവയിൽ നിന്ന്, നിയതേന്ദ്രിയത്തിലൂടെ ജ്ഞാനം ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്നു. ശബ്ദത്തിന്റെ ജ്ഞാനം ത്രിവിധസന്നികർഷത്തിൽ നിന്ന്; അത് ശ്രോത്രത്തിൽ സമവേതമാകയാൽ ശ്രോത്രേണ മാത്രം ഗ്രഹിക്കപ്പെടുന്നു. സംഖ്യ, പരിമാണം, പൃഥക്ത്വം, സംയോഗം, വിഭാഗം, പരത്വം, അപരത്വം, സ്നേഹം, ദ്രവത്വം, വേഗം, കർമ്മം — ഇവ പ്രത്യക്ഷദ്രവ്യങ്ങളിലെ സമവായത്താൽ ചക്ഷുസ്സും ത്വക്കും കൊണ്ട് ഗ്രഹിക്കപ്പെടുന്നു. ബുദ്ധി, സുഖം, ദുഃഖം, ഇച്ഛ, ദ്വേഷം, പ്രയത്നം — ഇവ ആത്മാവിന്റെയും മനസ്സിന്റെയും സംയോഗത്താൽ ഉപലബ്ധമാകുന്നു. ഭാവത്വം, ദ്രവ്യത്വം, ഗുണത്വം, കർമ്മത്വം മുതലായവ — അവയുടെ ആധാരത്തിൽ സമവേതമാകയാൽ — ആ ആധാരത്തെ ഗ്രഹിക്കുന്ന ഇന്ദ്രിയങ്ങൾ കൊണ്ടു തന്നെ ഗ്രഹിക്കപ്പെടുന്നു. ഇതാണു നമ്മെപ്പോലുള്ളവരുടെ പ്രത്യക്ഷം. എന്നാൽ നമ്മിൽനിന്ന് വിശിഷ്ടരായ യോഗികൾക്ക് — യുക്താവസ്ഥയിൽ — യോഗജധർമ്മം കൊണ്ട് അനുഗൃഹീതമായ മനസ്സിലൂടെ, സ്വാത്മാവ്, ഇതരാത്മാക്കൾ, ആകാശം, ദിക്, കാലം, പരമാണുക്കൾ, വായു, മനസ്സ്, അവയിലെ ഗുണ-കർമ്മ-സാമാന്യ-വിശേഷങ്ങൾ, സമവായം — എന്നിവയുടെ അവിതഥമായ സ്വരൂപദർശനം ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്നു. വിയുക്താവസ്ഥയിൽ, ചതുഷ്ടയസന്നികർഷത്തിൽനിന്ന് യോഗജധർമ്മാനുഗ്രഹസാമർത്ഥ്യം കൊണ്ട്, സൂക്ഷ്മവും വ്യവഹിതവും വിപ്രകൃഷ്ടവുമായ വസ്തുക്കളിൽ പ്രത്യക്ഷം ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്നു. സാമാന്യ-വിശേഷങ്ങളിൽ, പ്രമാണം സ്വരൂപാലോചനമാത്രം പ്രത്യക്ഷം; പ്രമേയങ്ങൾ ദ്രവ്യാദി പദാർത്ഥങ്ങൾ; പ്രമാതാവ് ആത്മാ; പ്രമിതി ദ്രവ്യാദിവിഷയമായ ജ്ഞാനം. അഥവാ — എല്ലാ പദാർത്ഥങ്ങളിലും ചതുഷ്ടയസന്നികർഷത്തിൽ നിന്ന് ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്ന അവിതഥവും അവ്യപദേശ്യവുമായ ജ്ഞാനമാണു പ്രത്യക്ഷം എന്നു പറയാം; പ്രമിതി ഇവിടെ ഗുണ-ദോഷ-മാധ്യസ്ഥ്യദർശനം.

en_simple_draft.text: Of these (four kinds of *vidyā*), that which arises from the *akṣa*s (sense-organs) is *pratyakṣa* — direct sensuous cognition. The *akṣa*s, i.e. the *indriya*s, are six: *ghrāṇa* (nose), *rasana* (tongue), *cakṣus* (eye), *tvak* (skin), *śrotra* (ear), and *manas* (the inner sense). This cognition arises with respect to *dravya* and the other categories. With respect to *dravya*, in its gross form composed of many parts, it arises from such causes as the manifestation of colour, the fourfold contact (*ātman*–*manas*–*indriya*–*viṣaya*), and the auxiliary presence of *dharma* etc.; here the cognition is in the form of mere *svarūpālocana* (perception of form). From the contact of *manas* qualified by *sāmānya*, *viśeṣa*, *dravya*, *guṇa* and *karma* with the *ātman*, *pratyakṣa* arises in the form 'this existent earthen white horned cow is moving.' With regard to *rūpa*, *rasa*, *gandha* and *sparśa*, the cognition arises through the relevant *indriya* from their *samavāya* in composite substances, their internal *viśeṣa*, and the contact with their substrate. The cognition of *śabda* arises through threefold contact, and being inherent in the ear is grasped by the ear alone. *Saṃkhyā*, *parimāṇa*, *pṛthaktva*, *saṃyoga*, *vibhāga*, *paratva*, *aparatva*, *sneha*, *dravatva*, *vega* and *karma* are grasped by *cakṣus* and *tvak* through their *samavāya* in perceptible substances. *Buddhi*, *sukha*, *duḥkha*, *icchā*, *dveṣa* and *prayatna* are grasped through the conjunction of *ātman* and *manas*. *Bhāvatva*, *dravyatva*, *guṇatva*, *karmatva* and the like — being inherent in cognisable substrates — are grasped by the same *indriya*s that grasp those substrates. This is the *pratyakṣa* of beings like ourselves. For those distinguished from us — i.e. *yogi*s in the *yukta* (ecstatic) state — through the *manas* assisted by faculties born of *yoga*, an unerring perception of the real form arises with respect to one's own *ātman*, other *ātman*s, *ākāśa*, *dik*, *kāla*, *paramāṇu*s, *vāyu*, *manas*, the *guṇa*-*karma*-*sāmānya*-*viśeṣa* inherent in these, and *samavāya*. For *yogi*s in the *viyukta* (out-of-ecstasy) state, through fourfold contact and the power of *yogaja-dharma*, *pratyakṣa* arises with respect to subtle, hidden and distant objects. With regard to *sāmānya* and *viśeṣa*, the *pramāṇa* (means of cognition) is mere *svarūpālocana*; the *prameya* (objects of cognition) are *dravya* and the other categories; the *pramātṛ* (cognising agent) is the *ātman*; and the *pramiti* (resultant cognition) is the knowledge of *dravya* etc. Or alternatively: *pratyakṣa* may be defined as any unerring and undeclared (*avyapadeśya*) cognition arising from fourfold contact with respect to all categories; here *pramiti* is the discernment of the good, bad and indifferent character of things.

sa_devanagari: लिङ्गदर्शनात् संजायमानं लैङ्गिकम् ॥ १०० ॥
sa_iast: liṅgadarśanāt saṃjāyamānaṃ laiṅgikam || 100 ||
literal_en: The laiṅgika, ‘inferential’ cognition is that which proceeds from, the sight or perception of the liṅga, mark or ‘probans’.

ml_draft.text: ലിംഗത്തിന്റെ ദർശനത്തിൽ നിന്ന് സംജായമാനമായ ജ്ഞാനമാണു ലൈംഗികം (അനുമാനജ്ഞാനം).

en_simple_draft.text: *Laiṅgika*, i.e. inferential cognition, is that which arises from the perception (*darśana*) of the *liṅga* — the indicative mark or 'probans'.

sa_devanagari:
लिङ्गं पुनः |
यदनुमेयेन सम्बद्धं प्रसिद्धं च तदन्विते |
तदभावे च नास्त्येव तल्लिङ्गमनुमापकम् ||
विपरीतमतो यत् स्यादेकेन द्वितयेन वा |
विरुद्धासिद्धसन्दिग्धमलिङ्गम् काश्यपो'ब्रवीत् ॥ १०१ ॥
sa_iast:
liṅgaṃ punaḥ |
yadanumeyena sambaddhaṃ prasiddhaṃ ca tadanvite |
tadabhāve ca nāstyeva talliṅgamanumāpakam ||
viparītamato yat syādekena dvitayena vā |
viruddhāsiddhasandigdhamaliṅgam kāśyapo'bravīt || 101 ||
literal_en:
The liṅga is that which is related to the object to be inferred, and is known to exist in that which is connected with that object, not existing in that wherein that is not present, such a liṅga is the means of inference.—(IX-ii-1).

That which is otherwise than this, being devoid of either one or both of these characteristics, is either ‘contradictory,’ or ‘unknown’ or ‘doubtful’; and is not a liṅga; so said Kāśyapa.

ml_draft.text: ലിംഗം എന്നതാകട്ടെ — അനുമേയത്തോടു സംബന്ധിച്ചു നില്ക്കുന്നതും, അനുമേയധർമ്മത്തോടു ചേർന്ന ഇതരവസ്തുക്കളിൽ പ്രസിദ്ധവും, അനുമേയത്തിന്റെ അഭാവത്തിൽ ഇല്ലാത്തതും — ഇതാണു അനുമാപകമായ ലിംഗം. ഈ ലക്ഷണത്തിന് വിപരീതമായി — ഈ രണ്ടു ധർമ്മങ്ങളിൽ ഏതെങ്കിലും ഒന്നോ രണ്ടും ഇല്ലാത്തത് — അത് വിരുദ്ധം, അസിദ്ധം, അല്ലെങ്കിൽ സന്ദിഗ്ധം ആകുന്നു; അത് ലിംഗമല്ല. ഇപ്രകാരം കാശ്യപൻ (കണാദൻ) പറഞ്ഞു.

en_simple_draft.text: The *liṅga* is what is related (*sambaddha*) to the *anumeya* (object to be inferred), known to exist in that which is connected with that object, and absent where the object is absent — such a *liṅga* is the *anumāpaka* (means of inference). What is otherwise — lacking either one or both of these characteristics — is *viruddha* (contrary), *asiddha* (unknown), or *sandigdha* (doubtful), and is no *liṅga*. So spoke Kāśyapa (Kaṇāda).

sa_devanagari: यदनुमेयेनार्थेन देशविशेषे कालविशेषे वा सहचरितम् अनुमेयधर्मान्विते चान्यत्र सर्वस्मिन्नेकदेशे वा प्रसिद्धम् अनुमेयविपरीते च सर्वस्मिन् प्रमाणतो'सद् एव तदप्रसिद्धार्थस्यानुमापकम् लिङ्गम् भवतीति ॥ १०२ ॥
sa_iast: yadanumeyenārthena deśaviśeṣe kālaviśeṣe vā sahacaritam anumeyadharmānvite cānyatra sarvasminnekadeśe vā prasiddham anumeyaviparīte ca sarvasmin pramāṇato'sad eva tadaprasiddhārthasyānumāpakam liṅgam bhavatīti || 102 ||
literal_en: (1) That which is concomitant, either in time or place, with the ‘object to be inferred,’—2 which is known io exist either in the whole or in a part of something endowed with the property of the inferred’,—and (3) which is authoritatively known to be non-existing in the whole of that which is contrary to the ‘object to be inferred’,—serves to bring about the inference of the unknown object, and it is ‘liṅga’ (Inferential Indicative).

ml_draft.text: (1) അനുമേയമായ അർത്ഥത്തോടൊപ്പം ദേശവിശേഷത്തിലോ കാലവിശേഷത്തിലോ സഹചരിക്കുന്നതും, (2) അനുമേയധർമ്മത്തോടു ചേർന്ന ഇതര വസ്തുവിൽ — അതിൻ്റെ സർവത്ര അല്ലെങ്കിൽ ഏകദേശത്തിൽ — പ്രസിദ്ധവും, (3) അനുമേയത്തിന് വിപരീതമായ വസ്തുക്കളിൽ സർവത്ര പ്രമാണം കൊണ്ട് അസത്തായതും ആയത് — അപ്രസിദ്ധാർത്ഥത്തിന്റെ അനുമാപകമായ ലിംഗം ആകുന്നു.

en_simple_draft.text: (1) That which is *sahacarita* (concomitant), in a particular *deśa* (place) or *kāla* (time), with the *anumeya* (object to be inferred), (2) which is *prasiddha* (well-known) — either wholly or in part — in another object endowed with the *dharma* of the *anumeya*, and (3) which by valid means of cognition is known to be wholly absent in everything contrary to the *anumeya*, — that becomes the *liṅga* which infers the unknown object.

sa_devanagari: यत्तु यथोक्तात् त्रिरूपाल्लिङ्गादेकेन धर्मेण द्वाभ्यां वा विपरीतं तदनुमेयस्याधिगमे लिङ्गं न भवतीत्येतदेवाह सूत्रकारः अप्रसिद्धोऽनपदेशोऽसन् सन्दिग्धश्चेति ॥ १०३ ॥
sa_iast: yattu yathoktāt trirūpālliṅgādekena dharmeṇa dvābhyāṃ vā viparītaṃ tadanumeyasyādhigame liṅgaṃ na bhavatītyetadevāha sūtrakāraḥ aprasiddho'napadeśo'san sandigdhaśceti || 103 ||
literal_en: That which differs from the above-mentioned ‘liṅga’ in one or both points is not a ‘liṅga’ (means) in the comprehension of the object to be inferred; this is what the author of the Sūtra has declared in the Sūtra ‘aprasiddho'napadeśo'san digdhaśca’—(Vaiśeṣika-Sūtra III-i-15).

ml_draft.text: മേല്പറഞ്ഞ ത്രിരൂപമായ ലിംഗത്തിൽ നിന്ന് ഒരു ധർമ്മത്തിലോ രണ്ടു ധർമ്മങ്ങളിലോ വിപരീതമായതെന്തോ — അത് അനുമേയത്തിന്റെ അധിഗമത്തിൽ ലിംഗമാകുന്നില്ല. ഇതാണു സൂത്രകാരൻ (കണാദൻ) പറഞ്ഞത്: 'അപ്രസിദ്ധനനപദേശോ'സന് സന്ദിഗ്ധശ്ച' എന്ന്.

en_simple_draft.text: That which differs from the above-described threefold *liṅga* in one or both characteristics is no *liṅga* in the apprehension of the *anumeya*. This is what the *sūtrakāra* (Kaṇāda) declares in the *sūtra* — 'aprasiddho'napadeśo'san sandigdhaśca' (Vaiśeṣika-Sūtra III-i-15).

sa_devanagari: विधिस्तु यत्र धूमस्तत्राग्निरग्न्यभावे धूमोऽपि न भवतीति । एवं प्रसिद्धसमयस्यासन्दिग्धधूमदर्शनात् साहचर्यानुस्मरणात् तदनन्तरम् अग्न्यध्यवसायो भवतीति । एवं सर्वत्र देशकालाविनाभूतम् इतरस्य लिङ्गम् । शास्त्रे कार्यादिग्रहणं निदर्शनार्थं कृतं नावधारणार्थं कस्माद्यूतिरेकदर्शनात् । तद्यथा अध्वर्युरोंश्रावयन् व्यवहितस्य होतुर्लिङ्गं चन्द्रोदयः समुद्रवृद्धेः कुमुदविकाशस्य च शरदि जलप्रसादोऽगस्त्योदयस्येति । एवमादि तत् सर्वम् अस्येदम् इति सम्बन्धमात्रवचनात् सिद्धम् । तत् तु द्विविधम् । दृष्टं सामान्यतो दृष्टं च । तत्र दृष्टं प्रसिद्धसाध्ययोरत्यन्तजात्यभेदेऽनुमानम् । यथा गव्येव सास्नामात्रम् उपलभ्य देशान्तरेऽपि सास्नामात्रदर्शनाद् गवि प्रतिपत्तिः । प्रसिद्धसाध्ययोरत्यन्तजातिभेदे लिङ्गानुमेयधर्मसामान्यानुवृत्तितोऽनुमानं सामान्यतो दृष्टम् । यथा कर्षकवणिग्राजपुरुषाणां च प्रवृत्तेः फलवत्त्वम् उपलभ्य वर्णाश्रमिणाम् अपि दृष्टं प्रयोजनम् अनुद्दिश्य प्रवर्तमानानां फलानुमानम् इति । तत्र लिङ्गदर्शनं प्रमाणं प्रमितिरग्निज्ञानम् । अथवाग्निज्ञानम् एव प्रमाणं प्रमितिरग्नौ गुणदोषमाध्यस्थ्यदर्शनम् इत्येतत् स्वनिश्चितार्थम् अनुमानम् ॥ १०४ ॥
sa_iast: vidhistu yatra dhūmastatrāgniragnyabhāve dhūmo'pi na bhavatīti | evaṃ prasiddhasamayasyāsandigdhadhūmadarśanāt sāhacaryānusmaraṇāt tadanantaram agnyadhyavasāyo bhavatīti | evaṃ sarvatra deśakālāvinābhūtam itarasya liṅgam | śāstre kāryādigrahaṇaṃ nidarśanārthaṃ kṛtaṃ nāvadhāraṇārthaṃ kasmādyūtirekadarśanāt | tadyathā adhvaryuroṃśrāvayan vyavahitasya hoturliṅgaṃ candrodayaḥ samudravṛddheḥ kumudavikāśasya ca śaradi jalaprasādo'gastyodayasyeti | evamādi tat sarvam asyedam iti sambandhamātravacanāt siddham | tat tu dvividham | dṛṣṭaṃ sāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ ca | tatra dṛṣṭaṃ prasiddhasādhyayoratyantajātyabhede'numānam | yathā gavyeva sāsnāmātram upalabhya deśāntare'pi sāsnāmātradarśanād gavi pratipattiḥ | prasiddhasādhyayoratyantajātibhede liṅgānumeyadharmasāmānyānuvṛttito'numānaṃ sāmānyato dṛṣṭam | yathā karṣakavaṇigrājapuruṣāṇāṃ ca pravṛtteḥ phalavattvam upalabhya varṇāśramiṇām api dṛṣṭaṃ prayojanam anuddiśya pravartamānānāṃ phalānumānam iti | tatra liṅgadarśanaṃ pramāṇaṃ pramitiragnijñānam | athavāgnijñānam eva pramāṇaṃ pramitiragnau guṇadoṣamādhyasthyadarśanam ityetat svaniścitārtham anumānam || 104 ||
literal_en:
The process (of inference) is as follows: ‘Whenever there is smoke there is fire; where there is no fire there is no smoke’—one whois cognisant of this concomitance, when he has an absolutely certain vision of smoke, he recalls to his mind its concomitance (with fire), after which comes the cognition of the presence of Are.—(IX-ii-1).

Thus in all cases when one thing is invariably concomitant with another in point of time and place, it becomes its ‘liṅga.’—(IX-ii-2).

In the Vaiśeṣika Sūtra, the author has mentioned ‘effect and the rest’ only with a view to exemplification, and not for the purposes of restriction. ‘How so?’ Because we find (Inferences) apart from those therein specified. For instance, the fact of the Adhvaryu priestrepeating ‘om’ is indicative of the presence of the Hotṛ priest; the rise of the moon is indicative of the rise in the sea, and also of the blooming of the water-lily; the clearness of water in the autumn is indicative of the rise of the constellation of Agastya.

These and such other inferences are all justified and pointed out by the expression ‘asyedam’ (in the Sūtra) which denotes mere relationship (of concomitance).—(III-i-9 to 14, III-i-7 to 8).

This Inference is of two kinds: (a) the Dṛṣṭa and (b) the Sāmānyatodṛṣṭa.’ The ‘Dṛṣṭa’ inference is that where the ‘prasiddha,’ that which is already known (as concomitant with the ‘liṅga,’), and the ‘sādhya,’ whose presence has to be proved, belong absolutely to the same class. As for instance, when one has seen the dewlap only in the body of the cow, whenever, on any subsequent occasion, he happens to see the dewlap, he infers the existence of the cow. When, however, the ‘prasiddha’ and the ‘sadhya’ belong to absolutely different classes, the inference follows only from the concomitance of the ‘generic form’ of the ‘liṅga’ with the ‘generic form’ of the ‘object to be inferred’; and this inference is called the ‘Sāmānyatodṛṣṭa’ As for instance, having found the activity of such persons, as the farmer, the trader and the servants of the king always leading to certain results, we infer the fact that, of persons observing the rites of their respective castes and conditions also, the activity, which is not found to have reference to any visible purpose, must tend to definite results.

In Inference, the ‘means of knowledge’ is the perception of the ‘liṅga,’ and the ‘knowledge’ is the cognition of fire; or the cognition of fire itself may be regarded as the means the ‘knowledge’ is the cognition of the good or indifferent character of the fire.

Such is the inference that serves the purposes of ones own definite cognition.—(II-i-8).

ml_draft.text: വിധി ഇപ്രകാരം: 'എവിടെ ധൂമം ഉണ്ടോ അവിടെ അഗ്നി ഉണ്ട്; അഗ്നിയുടെ അഭാവത്തിൽ ധൂമവും ഇല്ല.' — ഈ സഹചര്യത്തെ കുറിച്ച് സിദ്ധസമയനായ വ്യക്തി, അസന്ദിഗ്ധമായ ധൂമദർശനത്തിൽ നിന്ന് സാഹചര്യം അനുസ്മരിച്ച്, അനന്തരം 'ഇവിടെ അഗ്നി ഉണ്ട്' എന്ന അധ്യവസായം ചെയ്യുന്നു. ഇപ്രകാരം എല്ലായിടത്തും ദേശ-കാലങ്ങളിൽ അവിനാഭൂതമാണു മറ്റൊന്നിന്റെ ലിംഗം. ശാസ്ത്രത്തിൽ 'കാര്യാദി' എന്നു പറഞ്ഞത് നിദർശനത്തിന്നുവേണ്ടി മാത്രം, അവധാരണത്തിന്നല്ല — കാരണം മറ്റു ഇതരദർശനങ്ങളും ഉണ്ട്. ഉദാഹരണത്തിന്, അധ്വര്യു 'ഓം' ശ്രവിക്കുന്നത് വ്യവഹിതനായ ഹോതാവിന്റെ ലിംഗമാണ്; ചന്ദ്രോദയം സമുദ്രവൃദ്ധിയുടെയും കുമുദവികാസത്തിന്റെയും ലിംഗം; ശരത്കാലത്തെ ജലപ്രസാദം അഗസ്ത്യോദയത്തിന്റെ ലിംഗം. ഇത്തരം എല്ലാ അനുമാനങ്ങളും 'അസ്യേദം' (ഇതിന് ഇത്) എന്ന സംബന്ധമാത്രവചനത്താൽ സിദ്ധമാകുന്നു. ഈ അനുമാനം രണ്ടു വിധം — ദൃഷ്ടം, സാമാന്യതോദൃഷ്ടം. പ്രസിദ്ധവും സാധ്യവും അത്യന്തം ഒരേ ജാതിയിലുള്ളപ്പോൾ ദൃഷ്ടാനുമാനം. ഉദാ: പശുവിൽ മാത്രം സാസ്ന (തോൽ-മാല) കണ്ടവൻ, മറ്റു ദേശത്ത് വീണ്ടും സാസ്ന കണ്ട് അവിടെ പശുവിനെ പ്രതിപാദിക്കുന്നു. പ്രസിദ്ധവും സാധ്യവും വിഭിന്നജാതിയിലുള്ളപ്പോൾ — ലിംഗ-അനുമേയധർമ്മങ്ങളുടെ സാമാന്യാനുവൃത്തിയാൽ — അനുമാനം സാമാന്യതോദൃഷ്ടം. ഉദാ: കർഷകൻ, വണിക്ക്, രാജപുരുഷൻ — ഇവരുടെ പ്രവൃത്തി ഫലവത്താണെന്നു കണ്ട്, വർണ-ആശ്രമികളുടെ — ദൃഷ്ടപ്രയോജനം ലക്ഷ്യമാക്കാതെ പ്രവർത്തിക്കുന്നവരുടെ — കർമ്മത്തിനും ഫലം ഉണ്ടെന്നു അനുമാനിക്കുന്നു. ഇവിടെ ലിംഗദർശനം പ്രമാണം, പ്രമിതി അഗ്നിജ്ഞാനം. അഥവാ അഗ്നിജ്ഞാനം തന്നെ പ്രമാണം, പ്രമിതി അഗ്നിയിലെ ഗുണ-ദോഷ-മാധ്യസ്ഥ്യദർശനം — ഇതാണു സ്വനിശ്ചിതാർത്ഥമായ അനുമാനം.

en_simple_draft.text: The process (*vidhi*) of *anumāna* is as follows: 'wherever there is *dhūma* (smoke) there is *agni* (fire); where there is no *agni* there is no *dhūma*.' One who has firmly established this concomitance, having an undoubted perception of *dhūma* and recalling its concomitance, then arrives at the *adhyavasāya* 'fire is here.' Thus, in every case, that which is *avinābhūta* (invariably accompanying) something in time and place is its *liṅga*. In the *śāstra* (Kaṇāda's *sūtra*) the mention of 'effect etc.' is by way of illustration, not by way of restriction — because we find inferences beyond those listed. For instance, the *adhvaryu* priest's intoning of 'oṃ' is a *liṅga* of the presence of the (separated) *hotṛ* priest; the rising of the moon is a *liṅga* of the swelling of the sea and of the blooming of the lotus; the clarity of waters in autumn is a *liṅga* of the rising of Agastya. All such inferences are sanctioned by the expression *asyedam* ('this belongs to that') in the *sūtra*, which denotes mere relation. *Anumāna* is twofold: *dṛṣṭa* and *sāmānyatodṛṣṭa*. When the *prasiddha* and the *sādhya* (object to be proved) belong to absolutely the same class — the inference is *dṛṣṭa*. E.g., having seen the *sāsna* (dewlap) only on the cow, when one later perceives a *sāsna* elsewhere, one establishes the cow there. When the *prasiddha* and the *sādhya* belong to absolutely different classes — and the inference proceeds by the concomitance of the *sāmānya* (generic forms) of *liṅga* and *anumeya-dharma* — the inference is *sāmānyatodṛṣṭa*. E.g., having found that the activity of the farmer, trader and royal servant yields fruit, one infers that the activity of the *varṇa*-*āśrama*-bound persons — even when not aimed at any visible purpose — likewise yields fruit. Here the perception of the *liṅga* is the *pramāṇa*; the *pramiti* is the cognition of fire. Or, the cognition of fire itself is the *pramāṇa*; the *pramiti* is the discernment of the good, bad or indifferent character of the fire. This is *anumāna* serving the cognizer's own ascertainment.

sa_devanagari: शब्दादीनाम् अप्यनुमाने'न्तर्भावः समानविधित्वात् | यथा प्रसिद्धसमयस्यासन्दिग्धलिङ्गदर्शनप्रसिद्ध्यनुस्मरणाभ्याम् अतीन्द्रिये'र्थे भवत्यनुमानमेवं शब्दादिभ्यो'पीति | श्रुतिस्मृतिलक्षणो'प्याम्नायोवक्तृप्रामाण्यापेक्षः तद्वचनाद् आम्नायप्रामाण्यं लिङ्गाच्चानित्यो बुद्धिपूर्वा वाक्यकृतिर्वेदे बुद्धिपूर्वो ददातिरित्युक्तत्वात् ॥ १०५ ॥
sa_iast: śabdādīnām apyanumāne'ntarbhāvaḥ samānavidhitvāt | yathā prasiddhasamayasyāsandigdhaliṅgadarśanaprasiddhyanusmaraṇābhyām atīndriye'rthe bhavatyanumānamevaṃ śabdādibhyo'pīti | śrutismṛtilakṣaṇo'pyāmnāyovaktṛprāmāṇyāpekṣaḥ tadvacanād āmnāyaprāmāṇyaṃ liṅgāccānityo buddhipūrvā vākyakṛtirvede buddhipūrvo dadātirityuktatvāt || 105 ||
literal_en: Word, and the other means of knowledge, are included under ‘Inference’; because of the process of those being similar to that of Inferences Just as for one who is cognisant of the invariable concomitance, there arises, from the perception of an undoubted ‘liṅga’ and the remembranes of another concomitance, an inferential cognition of supersensuous things,—so in the same manner, does cognition arise from Word &c. also Scripture even in the form of śrutis and Smṛtis depends upon the authoritative character of the speaker; as the authority of the scripture rests upon his authority. And that Word is non-eternal is proved by inference:—‘the creation, of a sentence is due an intelligent action.,’ and ‘the word dadāti the Veda is preceded by intelligent action because, of its being spoken of as dadāti—(Vaiśeṣika Sūtras VI-i-1, 3).

ml_draft.text: ശബ്ദം മുതലായവയും അനുമാനത്തിൽ അന്തർഭാവം ചെയ്യുന്നു — സമാനവിധിയാകയാൽ. എങ്ങനെ എന്നാൽ — സിദ്ധസമയനായവന്, അസന്ദിഗ്ധലിംഗദർശനത്തിൽനിന്നും പ്രസിദ്ധിയുടെ അനുസ്മരണത്തിൽനിന്നും, അതീന്ദ്രിയമായ വസ്തുവിൽ അനുമാനം ഉണ്ടാകുന്നുവോ — അപ്രകാരം ശബ്ദാദികളിൽനിന്നും ഉണ്ടാകുന്നു. ശ്രുതി-സ്മൃതിസ്വരൂപമായ ആമ്നായവും വക്താവിന്റെ പ്രാമാണ്യാപേക്ഷയോടു കൂടിയതാണ്; തദ്വചനത്തിൽനിന്ന് ആമ്നായപ്രാമാണ്യം. ലിംഗത്തിൽനിന്ന് ശബ്ദം അനിത്യമെന്നു സിദ്ധിക്കുന്നു — 'ബുദ്ധിപൂർവം വാക്യകൃതി' (എന്നു സൂത്രം), 'വേദത്തിൽ ദദാതി ബുദ്ധിപൂർവം' എന്നു പറയപ്പെട്ടതിനാൽ.

en_simple_draft.text: *Śabda* (verbal testimony) and the other (alleged) means of cognition are subsumed under *anumāna*, since their procedure is the same. Just as, for one who is established in the *prasiddha* (invariable concomitance), there arises an *anumāna* concerning a supersensuous object from the perception of an undoubted *liṅga* and the recollection of the *prasiddha*, — so too does cognition arise from *śabda* etc. Even *āmnāya* (scripture) in the form of *śruti* and *smṛti* depends upon the authoritativeness of the speaker; from his utterance the authority of *āmnāya* follows. And from a *liṅga* it is established that *śabda* is non-eternal — for it has been said 'the production of a sentence is preceded by *buddhi* (intelligent action)' and 'in the Veda *dadāti* is preceded by *buddhi*' (Vaiśeṣika-Sūtras VI-i-1, 3).

sa_devanagari: प्रसिद्धाभिनयस्य चेष्टया प्रतिपत्तिदर्शनात् तद् अप्यनुमानम् एव ॥ १०६ ॥
sa_iast: prasiddhābhinayasya ceṣṭayā pratipattidarśanāt tad apyanumānam eva || 106 ||
literal_en: In as much as we find that it is only one to whom the signification of the gesture is known who has a cognition by means of the gesticulation, that cognition must be regarded as inferential.

ml_draft.text: പ്രസിദ്ധമായ അഭിനയത്തിന്റെ ചേഷ്ടയിലൂടെ പ്രതിപത്തി കാണുന്നത് കൊണ്ട് — അതും അനുമാനം തന്നെ ആകുന്നു.

en_simple_draft.text: Since we find that only one to whom the meaning of the *abhinaya* (gesture) is established attains cognition through the *ceṣṭā* (gesticulation), — that cognition too must be regarded as *anumāna*.

sa_devanagari: आप्तेनाप्रसिद्धस्य गवयस्य गवा गवयप्रतिपादनाद् उपमानम् आप्तवचनम् एव ॥ १०७ ॥
sa_iast: āptenāprasiddhasya gavayasya gavā gavayapratipādanād upamānam āptavacanam eva || 107 ||
literal_en: In as much as in the case of analogical cognition a trustworthy person describes the gavaya to one who does not know it, through the cow,—this must be regarded as a case of Trustworthy Assertion.

ml_draft.text: ആപ്തനായ ഒരാൾ, അപ്രസിദ്ധനായ ഗവയത്തെ, ഗോവിലൂടെ ഗവയത്തെ പ്രതിപാദിക്കുകയാൽ — ഉപമാനം ആപ്തവചനം തന്നെ ആകുന്നു.

en_simple_draft.text: Since, in the case of *upamāna* (analogical cognition), an *āpta* (trustworthy person) describes the *gavaya* — unknown to the hearer — through (its likeness to) the cow, — *upamāna* must be regarded as merely *āptavacana* (trustworthy assertion).

sa_devanagari: दर्शनार्थाद् अर्थापत्तिर्विरोध्येव श्रवणाद् अनुमितानुमानम् ॥ १०८ ॥
sa_iast: darśanārthād arthāpattirvirodhyeva śravaṇād anumitānumānam || 108 ||
literal_en: The Presumptive Cognition of a thing based upon a fact of perception is only ‘Inference per contraries’; and that based upon verbal cognition is an ‘Inference per Inference.’

ml_draft.text: ദർശനാർത്ഥത്തിൽനിന്ന് ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്ന അർത്ഥാപത്തി വിരോധി തന്നെ — അനുമാനത്തിന്റെ വിപരീതരീതി. ശ്രവണത്തിൽനിന്ന് ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്നത് അനുമിതാനുമാനം — അനുമാനത്തിൽനിന്നുള്ള അനുമാനം.

en_simple_draft.text: *Arthāpatti* (presumptive cognition) based on a fact of perception is only *anumāna* by contraries (*virodhi*); and that based upon what is heard (verbal cognition) is *anumitānumāna* — an inference based upon an inference.

sa_devanagari: सम्भवोऽप्यविनाभावित्वाद् अनुमानम् एव ॥ १०९ ॥
sa_iast: sambhavo'pyavinābhāvitvād anumānam eva || 109 ||
literal_en: Probability also, following from invariable concomitance, is a form of Inference—(IX-ii-5).

ml_draft.text: സംഭവവും — അവിനാഭാവിത്വം കൊണ്ട് — അനുമാനം തന്നെ ആകുന്നു.

en_simple_draft.text: *Sambhava* (probability), since it follows from *avinābhāva* (invariable concomitance), is itself a form of *anumāna*.

sa_devanagari: अभावोऽप्यनुमानम् एव यथोत्पन्नं कार्यं कारणसद्भावे लिङ्गम् । एवम् अनुत्पन्नं कार्यं कारणासद्भावे लिङ्गम् ॥ ११० ॥
sa_iast: abhāvo'pyanumānam eva yathotpannaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇasadbhāve liṅgam | evam anutpannaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇāsadbhāve liṅgam || 110 ||
literal_en: Negation also is mere Inference just as the appearance of the effect becomes ‘indicative’ of the existence of the cause, so also does the non-appearance of the effect become ‘indicative’ of the non-existence of the cause.—(IX-ii-5)

ml_draft.text: അഭാവവും അനുമാനം തന്നെ. എപ്രകാരം ഉത്ഭൂതമായ കാര്യം കാരണത്തിന്റെ സദ്ഭാവത്തിന്റെ ലിംഗമാകുന്നുവോ, അപ്രകാരം അനുത്ഭൂതമായ കാര്യം കാരണത്തിന്റെ അസദ്ഭാവത്തിന്റെ ലിംഗമാകുന്നു.

en_simple_draft.text: *Abhāva* (negation) too is mere *anumāna*. Just as the appearing of the *kārya* (effect) becomes the *liṅga* indicating the *sadbhāva* (existence) of the *kāraṇa* (cause), so the non-appearing of the *kārya* becomes the *liṅga* indicating the *asadbhāva* (non-existence) of the *kāraṇa*.

sa_devanagari: तथैवैतिह्यम् अप्यवितथम् आप्तोपदेश एवेति ॥ १११ ॥
sa_iast: tathaivaitihyam apyavitatham āptopadeśa eveti || 111 ||
literal_en: Similarly Tradition also, when true, is only Trustworthy Assertion.—(IX-ii-5).

ml_draft.text: അപ്രകാരം ഐതിഹ്യവും — അവിതഥമെങ്കിൽ — ആപ്തോപദേശം തന്നെ ആകുന്നു.

en_simple_draft.text: Similarly *aitihya* (tradition), when *avitatha* (true), is only *āptopadeśa* (trustworthy assertion).

sa_devanagari: पञ्चावयवेन वाक्येन स्वनिश्चितार्थप्रतिपादनां परार्थानुमानम् | पञ्चावयवेनैव वाक्येन संशयितविपर्यस् ताव्युत्पन्नानां परेषां स्वनिश्चितार्थप्रतिपादनं परार्थानुमानं विज्ञेयम् ॥ ११२ ॥
sa_iast: pañcāvayavena vākyena svaniścitārthapratipādanāṃ parārthānumānam | pañcāvayavenaiva vākyena saṃśayitaviparyas tāvyutpannānāṃ pareṣāṃ svaniścitārthapratipādanaṃ parārthānumānaṃ vijñeyam || 112 ||
literal_en: Inference ‘for the benefit of others’ consists in the expounding of something known to the person himself, by means of a ‘five-membered’ sentence. That is to say, when by means of the five-membered sentence a man expounds what he himself knows to be absolutely true, to other persons, who have either a doubtful or a mistaken idea about the thing, or have no knowledge of it at all,—then we have what is called ‘Inference for the benefit of others.’—(XI-ii-1)

ml_draft.text: പഞ്ചാവയവ-വാക്യത്താൽ സ്വനിശ്ചിതാർത്ഥത്തെ പ്രതിപാദിക്കുന്നതാണു പരാർത്ഥാനുമാനം. അതായത് — സംശയിതരോ, വിപര്യസ്തരോ, അവ്യുത്പന്നരോ ആയ പരർക്ക്, പഞ്ചാവയവവാക്യത്താൽത്തന്നെ സ്വനിശ്ചിതാർത്ഥത്തെ പ്രതിപാദിക്കുന്നതാണു പരാർത്ഥാനുമാനം എന്നു അറിയണം.

en_simple_draft.text: *Parārthānumāna* — inference 'for the sake of others' — consists in the expounding of an *artha* (matter) ascertained by oneself, by means of a *pañcāvayava* (five-membered) sentence. That is to say, when by means of a five-membered sentence one expounds, to others who are doubtful, mistaken, or unlearned, an *artha* known to oneself for certain, — that is to be known as *parārthānumāna*.

sa_devanagari: अवयवाः पुनः प्रतिज्ञापदेशनिदर्शनानुसन्धानप्रत्याम्नायाः । तत्रानुमेयोद्देशोऽविरोधी प्रतिज्ञा । प्रतिपिपादयिषितधर्मविशिष्टस्य धर्मिणोपदेशविषयम् आपादयितुम् उद्देशमात्रं प्रतिज्ञा । यथा द्रव्यं वायुरिति । अविरोधिग्रहणात् प्रत्यक्षानुमानाभ्युपगतस्वशास्त्रस्ववचनविरोधिनो निरस्ता भवन्ति । यथाऽनुष्णोऽग्निरिति प्रत्यक्षविरोधी घनम् अम्बरम् इत्यनुमानविरोधी ब्राह्मणेन सुरा पेयेत्यागमविरोधी वैशेषिकस्य सत्कार्यम् इतिब्रुवतः स्वशास्त्रविरोधी न शब्दोऽर्थप्रत्यायक इति स्ववचनविरोधी ॥ ११३ ॥
sa_iast: avayavāḥ punaḥ pratijñāpadeśanidarśanānusandhānapratyāmnāyāḥ | tatrānumeyoddeśo'virodhī pratijñā | pratipipādayiṣitadharmaviśiṣṭasya dharmiṇopadeśaviṣayam āpādayitum uddeśamātraṃ pratijñā | yathā dravyaṃ vāyuriti | avirodhigrahaṇāt pratyakṣānumānābhyupagatasvaśāstrasvavacanavirodhino nirastā bhavanti | yathā'nuṣṇo'gniriti pratyakṣavirodhī ghanam ambaram ityanumānavirodhī brāhmaṇena surā peyetyāgamavirodhī vaiśeṣikasya satkāryam itibruvataḥ svaśāstravirodhī na śabdo'rthapratyāyaka iti svavacanavirodhī || 113 ||
literal_en:
These members are—(1) Pratijñā, ‘Declaration,’ Proposition to be proved (2) Apadeśa, Statement of the inferential indicative or ‘middle term’ (3) Nidarśana, ‘Statement of the Major Premiss,’ (4) Anusandhāna, ‘Statement of the Minor Premiss,’ and (5) Pratyāmnāya, ‘Reiteration of the Conclusion’.

Of these (1) the Conclusion is the statement of what is to be proved by means of the inference, and which is not incompatible with facts. That is to say, it consists in the mere statement of the ‘subject’ endowed with the property sought to be proved, with a view to point out the substratum of the ‘indicative.’ As an example of this we have the proposition ‘Wind is a substance.’—(IX-ii-1).

The qualification ‘not incompatible, &c.’ serves the purpose of excluding such propositions as may be contrary to (1) Sense-cognition, (2) Inference, (3) Scriptures regarded as trustworthy by the speaker, (4) that which would involve a self-contradiction,; e. g. the proposition ‘Fire is not hot,’ would be contrary, to sense-cognition (1); (2) that ‘ākāśa’ is dense would be contrary to Inference; (3) that ‘the Brāhmaṇa ought to drink wine’ would be ‘contrary to scriptures’; and that ‘the effect is ever existing’ would, for the Vaiśeṣika, be contrary to his own theory; and (4) that ‘word is not expressive’ would involve a self-contradiction.—(III-i-15).

ml_draft.text: അവയവങ്ങളാകട്ടെ — പ്രതിജ്ഞ, അപദേശം, നിദർശനം, അനുസന്ധാനം, പ്രത്യാമ്നായം എന്നിവ. ഇതിൽ അനുമേയത്തിന്റെ അവിരോധിയായ ഉദ്ദേശമാണു പ്രതിജ്ഞ. പ്രതിപാദിക്കാൻ ആഗ്രഹിച്ച ധർമ്മത്തോടു കൂടിയ ധർമ്മിയെ ഉപദേശവിഷയമായി ആപാദിപ്പിക്കാൻ വേണ്ടി ഉദ്ദേശമാത്രം — ഇതാണു പ്രതിജ്ഞ. ഉദാഹരണത്തിന് 'വായു ദ്രവ്യമാണ്' എന്നത്. 'അവിരോധി' എന്ന വിശേഷണത്താൽ — പ്രത്യക്ഷം, അനുമാനം, ആഗമം, സ്വശാസ്ത്രം, സ്വവചനം എന്നിവയോട് വിരോധിയായ പ്രതിജ്ഞകൾ നിരസിക്കപ്പെടുന്നു. 'അനുഷ്ണനഗ്നി' എന്നത് പ്രത്യക്ഷവിരോധി; 'ഘനമംബരം' എന്നത് അനുമാനവിരോധി; 'ബ്രാഹ്മണൻ സുര കുടിക്കണം' എന്നത് ആഗമവിരോധി; 'സത്കാര്യം' എന്നു വൈശേഷികൻ പറഞ്ഞാൽ സ്വശാസ്ത്രവിരോധി; 'ശബ്ദം അർത്ഥപ്രത്യായകം അല്ല' എന്നത് സ്വവചനവിരോധി.

en_simple_draft.text: The *avayava*s (members of the syllogism) are: *pratijñā* (declaration / proposition), *apadeśa* (statement of the inferential indicative or 'middle term'), *nidarśana* (statement of the major premiss), *anusandhāna* (statement of the minor premiss), and *pratyāmnāya* (reiteration of the conclusion). Among these, *pratijñā* is the *uddeśa* (statement) — not incompatible (*avirodhī*) with facts — of the *anumeya* (object to be inferred). It consists in the mere statement of the *dharmin* (subject) qualified by the *dharma* (property) one wishes to prove, in order to bring it forth as the substratum of the *upadeśa* of the *liṅga*. As an example: 'wind is a *dravya*.' By the qualification 'not incompatible' are excluded propositions opposed to *pratyakṣa*, *anumāna*, *āgama* (scripture accepted by oneself), *svaśāstra* (one's own *darśana*'s tenets), and *svavacana* (one's own statement). E.g., 'fire is not hot' is opposed to *pratyakṣa*; 'the sky is dense' is opposed to *anumāna*; 'a *brāhmaṇa* should drink wine' is opposed to *āgama*; 'effect already exists' (*satkārya*), if asserted by a *vaiśeṣika*, is opposed to *svaśāstra*; 'a word does not convey meaning' is opposed to *svavacana*.

sa_devanagari: लिङ्गवचनम् अपदेशः । यदनुमेयेन सहचरितम् तत्समानजातीये सर्वत्र सामान्येन प्रसिद्धं तद्विपरीते च सर्वस्मिन्नसद् एव तल्लिङ्गम् उक्तम् तस्य वचनम् अपदेशः । यथा क्रियावत्त्वाद् गुणवत्त्वाच्च तथा च तदनुमेयेऽस्ति तत्समानजातीये च सर्वस्मिन् गुणवत्त्वम् असार्वस्मिन् क्रियावत्त्वम् । उभयम् अप्येतद् अद्रव्ये नास्त्येव तस्मात् तस्य वचनम् अपदेश इति सिद्धम् ॥ ११४ ॥
sa_iast: liṅgavacanam apadeśaḥ | yadanumeyena sahacaritam tatsamānajātīye sarvatra sāmānyena prasiddhaṃ tadviparīte ca sarvasminnasad eva talliṅgam uktam tasya vacanam apadeśaḥ | yathā kriyāvattvād guṇavattvācca tathā ca tadanumeye'sti tatsamānajātīye ca sarvasmin guṇavattvam asārvasmin kriyāvattvam | ubhayam apyetad adravye nāstyeva tasmāt tasya vacanam apadeśa iti siddham || 114 ||
literal_en: The ‘Apadeśa’ consists in the statement of the ‘inferential indicative.’ That which is concomitant with the ‘subject’ of inference, being known to be so concomitant at all times, and with all individuals of the class to which the ‘subject’ belongs,—and which, at all times, is never concomitant with the contradictory of that subject,—has been spoken of as the ‘inferential indicative’; and it is the statement or putting forward of this that constitutes ‘apadeśa.’ As for instance (in the same argument) the assertion—‘because wind has an action and is endowed with certain qualities’ Here we find that ‘action’ and ‘quality’ exist in the ‘subject’ (the wind), and the latter in all individuals of the class to which it belongs, and the former not in all of them and both of these are never found in anything that is ‘not substance.’ Hence the statement as to the presence of these in wind constitutes the ‘apadeśa’ (in the argument cited).—(IX.ii.1)

ml_draft.text: ലിംഗവചനം അപദേശം. അനുമേയത്തോടു സഹചരിതവും, അതിന്റെ സമാനജാതിയിലുള്ള എല്ലാറ്റിലും സാമാന്യേന പ്രസിദ്ധവും, അതിന്റെ വിപരീതത്തിൽ ഒന്നിലും അസത്തായതും — ഇതാണു ലിംഗം എന്ന് ഉപര്യപി പറഞ്ഞത്; ആ ലിംഗത്തിന്റെ വചനമാണു അപദേശം. ഉദാ: 'ക്രിയാവത്ത്വാദ് ഗുണവത്ത്വാച്ച' എന്നത്. ഇപ്രകാരം — അനുമേയത്തിൽ (വായുവിൽ) അവ ഉണ്ട്; സമാനജാതിയിലുള്ള എല്ലാറ്റിലും ഗുണവത്ത്വം ഉണ്ട്, എല്ലാറ്റിലുമല്ലെങ്കിലും ക്രിയാവത്ത്വവും ഉണ്ട്. ഈ രണ്ടും അദ്രവ്യത്തിൽ ഇല്ല തന്നെ. അതിനാൽ അവയുടെ വചനം അപദേശമാകുന്നു — ഇത് സിദ്ധം.

en_simple_draft.text: *Apadeśa* consists in the *vacana* (statement) of the *liṅga*. That which is *sahacarita* (concomitant) with the *anumeya*, generally established in all individuals of the same class, and absent in everything contrary — that has been called the *liṅga*; its statement is *apadeśa*. E.g. (in the same argument): 'because (wind) has *kriyā* (action) and possesses *guṇa*.' Thus *kriyāvattva* (possession of action) and *guṇavattva* (possession of quality) exist in the *anumeya* (wind); *guṇavattva* exists in all individuals of the same class, and *kriyāvattva* in some of them; both, however, are wholly absent in *adravya* (non-substance). Hence the statement of these constitutes *apadeśa*.

sa_devanagari: एतेनासिद्धविरुद्धसन्दिग्धानध्यवसितवचनानाम् अनपदेशत्वम् उक्तम् भवति । तत्रासिद्धश्चतुर्विधः । उभयासिद्धोऽन्यतरासिद्धः तद्भावासिद्धोऽनुमेयासिद्धश्चेति । तत्रोभयासिद्धः उभयोर्वादिप्रतिवादिनोरसिद्धः यथाऽनित्यः शब्दः सावयवत्वाद् इति ।अन्यतरासिद्धः यथाऽनित्यः शब्दः कार्यत्वाद् इति । तद्भावासिद्धो यथा धूमभावेनाग्न्यधिगतौ कर्तव्यायाम् उपन्यस्यमानो वाष्पे धूमभावेनासिद्ध इति । अनुमेयासिद्धो यथा पार्थिवम् द्रव्यम् तमः कृष्णरूपवत्त्वाद् इति । यो ह्यनुमेयेऽविद्यमानोऽपि तत्समानजातीये सर्वस्मिन् नास्ति तद्विपरीते चास्ति स विपरीतसाधनाद् विरुद्धः यथा यस्माद् विषाणी तस्माद् अश्व इति । यस्तु सन्ननुमेये तत्समानासमानजातीययोः साधारणः सन्नेव स सन्देहजनकत्वात् सन्दिग्धः यथा यस्माद् विषाणी तस्माद् गौरिति । एकस्मिंश्च द्वयोर्हेत्वोर्यथोक्तलक्षणयोर्विरुद्धयोः सन्निपाते सति संशयदर्शनाद् अयम् अन्यः सन्दिग्ध इति केचित् । यथा मूर्तत्वामूर्तत्वम् प्रति मनसः क्रियावत्त्वास्पर्शवत्त्वयोरिति । नन्वयम् असाधारण एवाचाक्षुषत्वप्रत्यक्षत्ववत् संहतयोरन्यतरपक्षासम्भवात् ततश्चानध्यवसित इत् वक्ष्यामः । ननु शास्त्रे तत्रतत्रोभयथा दर्शनम् संशयकारणम् अपदिश्यत इति न संशयो विषयद्वैतदर्शनात् । संशयोत्पत्तौ विषयद्वैतदर्शनम् कारणम् तुल्यबलत्वे च तयोः परस्परविरोधान् निर्णयानुत्पादकत्वम् स्यान् न तु संशयहेतुत्वम् न च तयोस्तुल्यबलवत्त्वम् अस्ति अन्यतरस्यानुमेयोद्देशस्यागमबाधितत्वाद् अयम् तु विरुद्धभेद एव । यश्चानुमेये विद्यमानस्तत्समानासमानजातीययोरसन्नेव सोऽन्यतरासिद्धोऽनध्यवसायहेतुत्वाद् अनध्यवसितः यथा सत्कार्यम् उत्पत्तेरिति । अयम् अप्रसिद्धोऽनपदेश इति वचनाद् अवरुद्धः । ननु चायम् विशेषः संशयहेतुरभिहितः शास्त्रे तुल्यजातीयेष्वर्थान्तरभूतेषु विशेषस्योभयथा दृष्टत्वाद् इति नान्यार्थत्वाच्छब्दे विशेषदर्शनात् । संशयानुत्पत्तिरित्युक्ते नायम् द्रव्यादीनाम् अन्यतमस्य विशेषः स्याच्छ्रावणत्वम् किम् तु सामान्यम् एव सम्पद्यते कस्मात् तुल्यजातीयेष्वर्थान्तरभूतेषु द्रव्यादिभेदानाम् एकैकशो विशेषस्योभयथा दृष्टत्वाद् इत्युक्तम् न संशयकारणम् अन्यथा षट्स्वपि पदार्थेषु संशयप्रसङ्गात् तस्मात् सामान्यप्रत्ययाद् एव संशय इति ॥ ११५ ॥

literal_en:
By this it is implied that such statements as are either (1) ‘asiddha’ (unknown, unproved), or (2) ‘viruddha’ (contrary), or (3) ‘sandigdha’ (doubtful), or (4) ‘anadhyavasita’ (unascertained), have not the character of the true ‘reason’ (or ‘indicative’).

(1) Of these the ‘unknown’ is of four kinds—(a) ‘unknown to both,’ (b) ‘unknown to one of the two,’ (c) unknown in the form wanted, and (d) ‘the unknown—subject-of-inference.’ (a) The ‘unknown to both’ is that which is not known to both the arguer and the person to whom the argument is presented; e.g., the argument—‘sound is evanescent, because it is made up of parts.’ (b) As an example of the ‘unknown to one of the two,’ we have—‘sound is evanescent because it is an effect,’ (c) We have the ‘unknown in the form wanted’ when what is meant to be iṇḍicated is fire by the presence of smoke, but what is put forward us the ‘reason’ is steam, which is not known in the form of smoke, (d) We have the ‘unknown—subject-of-inference’ in the argument—‘Darkness in an earthy substance, because it is black in colour.’

(2) That which, while not subsisting in the subject of inference, does not subsist in any individual of the same class, and subsists in its contradictories,—is what is known as the ‘viruddha,’ ‘contrary’ reason, as ii proves something quite; contrary to the desired conclusion; as an examaple of this we have the reasoning—‘This animal is a horse, because it has horns.’

(3) That Which, while subsisting in the object of inference, subsists in things of the same kind as that as well as in those of other kinds, is what is known as ‘sandigdha,’ ‘Doubtful;’ as it creates a doubt in the mind; e.g., ‘this animal is a cow, because it has horns.’ Some people hold that when in any subject there is a collision of two ‘contrary’ indicatives explained above, there arises a doubt; and this is another kind of the ‘Doubtful’ reason; as for example in regard to the mind we find that the two reasons—(1) ‘because it has motion’ and (2) ‘because it cannot be felt by touch’—are put forward as indicative of its corporeal and non-corporeal character respectively.

Objection: “This would be a case of the ‘asādhāraṇa’ reason; because the two reasons cannot reside together either in the ‘subject’ or in its contradictory,—just like ‘non-visibility’ and ‘perceptibility.”

Reply: We shall explain later on that for this very reason the reasoning in question is what is known as the ‘anadhyavasita,’ ‘unascertained.’

Objection: “In the scriptures (the Sūtras) we find it mentioned in many places that two contrary cognitions constitute the cause of doubt.”

Reply: Not so; as doubts always arise from the dual perception of objects. That is to say, a Doubt is always produced by the perception of the dual character of an object; and when both factors of the duality would be of equal authority, they would contradict each other; and as such would not give rise to any definite cognition; but they could not be the cause of any doubt; as a matter of fact, in the instance cited, there is no equality of authority in the two factors of the duality; as one of the two conclusions of the inference would always be such as is denied by the scriptures; and hence this (that has been put forward as an instance of another kind of the ‘doubtful’ reason) would be only another kind of the ‘contrary’ reason.

(4) That which subsists in the ‘subject’ of the inference, but not in any other object either of the same kind or any other, is one that is not recognised by either party; and as such, giving rise to uncertainty, incomes to be known as the ‘unascertained’ reason; as for instance—‘the effect is an entity, because it is produced. This is implied in the Sūtra—‘aprasiddhonapadeśaḥ.’

Objection: “This distinctive feature has been spoken of in the scriptures as the cause of doubt; and the reason for this is that the distinctive feature of a thing serves to distinguish it from like as well as unlike objects, (and hence the ‘unascertained,’ comes within the Sūtra that speaks of the ‘sandigdha,’ and not within that which speaks of the ‘aprasiddha’ (‘unknown’).”

Reply: Not so; because of the meaning (of the sūtra) being different. That is to say, (the author of the Sūtra having made the declaration that there arises a doubt as to whether the audible object, sound, is a substance, or a quality or an action)’—the opponent has retorted that, in as much as the distinctive feature (of audibility) is found in sound alone, there can be no doubt; and to this the author of the sūtra has replied by pointing out that the distinctive feature of ‘audibility’ does not belong specifically to either the: Substance alone, or to the Quality alone, or to Action alone; in fact, it is common among all these; as in each of these three (substance, quality and action) we find distinctive features that distinguish them from like as well as unlike objects; (and for this same reason, ‘audibility’ also would be a feature that would belong in common to substance, quality and action; and hence it would not give rise to a doubt); and thus what the sūtra has done is to paint out (that in the said manner, ‘audibility’ might very well be regarded as leading to an uncertainty or doubt) and not that a distinctive feature becomes a cause or source of doubt. For, if it were not, then, there would be doubts with regard to all the six categories. For these reasons we conclude that Doubts always arise from the cognition of features common to more than one thing.

ml_draft.text: ഇതുകൊണ്ട് — അസിദ്ധം, വിരുദ്ധം, സന്ദിഗ്ധം, അനധ്യവസിതം എന്നീ വചനങ്ങൾക്ക് അനപദേശത്വം — ലിംഗത്വം ഇല്ലെന്ന് — പറഞ്ഞതായി. ഇതിൽ അസിദ്ധം നാലുവിധം — ഉഭയാസിദ്ധം, അന്യതരാസിദ്ധം, തദ്ഭാവാസിദ്ധം, അനുമേയാസിദ്ധം എന്നിങ്ങനെ. ഉഭയാസിദ്ധം — വാദി-പ്രതിവാദികൾ ഇരുവർക്കും അസിദ്ധം; ഉദാ: 'ശബ്ദം അനിത്യം, സാവയവത്വാത്' (ശബ്ദത്തിന്റെ സാവയവത്വം ഇരുവർക്കും അസിദ്ധം). അന്യതരാസിദ്ധം — ഉദാ: 'ശബ്ദം അനിത്യം, കാര്യത്വാത്' (മീമാംസകന് കാര്യത്വം അസിദ്ധം). തദ്ഭാവാസിദ്ധം — ഉദാ: ധൂമത്തിലൂടെ അഗ്നിയെ അനുമിക്കാൻ ഉദ്യമിക്കുന്നവൻ ബാഷ്പത്തെ ധൂമത്തിന്റെ ഭാവത്തിൽ ഉപന്യസിക്കുമ്പോൾ — അവിടെ 'ധൂമഭാവ'ം അസിദ്ധമാകുന്നു. അനുമേയാസിദ്ധം — ഉദാ: 'തമസ്സ് പാർത്ഥിവദ്രവ്യമാണ്, കൃഷ്ണരൂപവത്ത്വാത്' (തമസ്സ് ദ്രവ്യമാണെന്നു തന്നെ അസിദ്ധം). അനുമേയത്തിൽ ഇല്ലാത്തതും അതിന്റെ സമാനജാതിയിൽ ഒന്നിലും ഇല്ലാത്തതും വിപരീതത്തിൽ ഉള്ളതുമായ ലിംഗം — അത് വിപരീതസാധനത്താൽ വിരുദ്ധം. ഉദാ: 'വിഷാണിയാകയാൽ ഇതൊരു അശ്വം'. അനുമേയത്തിൽ ഉണ്ടെങ്കിലും അതിന്റെ സമാനവും അസമാനവുമായ ജാതികളിൽ സാധാരണമായി ഉള്ളത് — സന്ദേഹജനകത്വം കൊണ്ട് സന്ദിഗ്ധം. ഉദാ: 'വിഷാണിയാകയാൽ ഇതൊരു പശു'. ഒരേ വിഷയത്തിൽ വിരുദ്ധലക്ഷണങ്ങളുള്ള രണ്ടു ഹേതുക്കൾ സന്നിപതിക്കുമ്പോൾ സംശയം ഉണ്ടാകുന്നു — ഇത് മറ്റൊരുവിധം സന്ദിഗ്ധം എന്നു ചിലർ. ഉദാ: മനസ്സിന്റെ മൂർത്തത്വ-അമൂർത്തത്വങ്ങളെ കുറിച്ച് — 'ക്രിയാവത്ത്വാത്' / 'അസ്പർശവത്ത്വാത്' എന്നു യഥാക്രമം. എന്നാൽ ഇത് അസാധാരണം മാത്രം — സംഹതങ്ങളായവയിലെ അന്യതരപക്ഷാസംഭവം കൊണ്ട് — അനധ്യവസിതമെന്നു പറയാം. വാസ്തവത്തിൽ ശാസ്ത്രത്തിൽ വിഷയദ്വൈതദർശനം സംശയകാരണം എന്നു പറഞ്ഞത് — ഇത് വിരുദ്ധഭേദം മാത്രം ആകുന്നു; തുല്യബലത്വം ഇവയിൽ ഇല്ല — ഒരുവശം ആഗമബാധിതം. അനുമേയത്തിൽ ഉണ്ടെങ്കിലും സമാന-അസമാനജാതികളിൽ ഇല്ലാത്തത് — അനധ്യവസിതം. ഉദാ: 'സത്കാര്യം ഉത്പത്തേഃ' — ഇത് 'അപ്രസിദ്ധനനപദേശഃ' എന്ന വചനത്താൽ അവരുദ്ധം.

en_simple_draft.text: By this it is implied that statements which are *asiddha* (unknown, unproved), *viruddha* (contrary), *sandigdha* (doubtful), or *anadhyavasita* (unascertained) lack the character of *apadeśa*. (1) *Asiddha* is fourfold: *ubhayāsiddha* (unknown to both parties), *anyatarāsiddha* (unknown to one of the two), *tadbhāvāsiddha* (unknown in the form wanted), and *anumeyāsiddha* (the *anumeya* itself unknown). (a) *Ubhayāsiddha*: e.g. 'sound is *anitya* (non-eternal), because it is *sāvayava* (made of parts)' — both parties reject the premise. (b) *Anyatarāsiddha*: e.g. 'sound is *anitya*, because it is *kārya* (an effect)' — one party rejects. (c) *Tadbhāvāsiddha*: when one wishing to infer *agni* through *dhūma* puts forward steam (*vāṣpa*) as if it were *dhūma*. (d) *Anumeyāsiddha*: e.g. 'darkness is an earthen *dravya*, because it has *kṛṣṇarūpa* (black colour)' — but darkness's being a *dravya* is itself unknown. (2) *Viruddha*: that which, while not residing in the *anumeya*, also does not reside in any individual of its class but does reside in its contradictories — proving the contrary, e.g. 'this is a horse, because it has horns.' (3) *Sandigdha*: that which, while residing in the *anumeya*, is common to both *samānajātīya* and *asamānajātīya* — generating doubt, e.g. 'this is a cow, because it has horns.' Some hold that when in one subject two contrary *hetu*s of the said description meet — there arises doubt, and this is another kind of *sandigdha*. E.g. concerning *manas*'s *mūrtatva* and *amūrtatva*: '*kriyāvattva*' on one side and '*asparśavattva*' on the other. We shall later show that this is rather *asādhāraṇa* (unique-to-the-subject) and hence *anadhyavasita*, since for tightly-bound contraries one of the two alternatives cannot obtain. The *śāstra*'s mention of dual perception as a cause of doubt does not contradict this; for in such cases the two factors are not of equal authority — one is set aside by *āgama* — and so this reduces to a kind of *viruddha*. (4) *Anadhyavasita*: that which, while residing in the *anumeya*, resides neither in *samānajātīya* nor in *asamānajātīya* — being unrecognised by either party, it generates *anadhyavasāya*. E.g. '*satkārya*, because of *utpatti*' — this is already excluded by the dictum 'aprasiddho'napadeśaḥ.'

sa_devanagari: द्विविधं निदर्शनं साधर्म्येण वैधर्म्येण च । तत्रानुमेयसामान्येन लिङ्गसामान्यस्यानुविधानदर्शनं साधर्म्यनिदर्शनम् । तद्यथा यत् क्रियावत् तद् द्रव्यं दृष्टं यथा शर इति । अनुमेयविपर्यये च लिङ्गस्याभावदर्शनं वैधर्म्यनिदर्शनम् । तद्यथा यद् अद्रव्यं तत् क्रियावन् न भवति यथा सत्तेति ॥ ११६ ॥
sa_iast: dvividhaṃ nidarśanaṃ sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa ca | tatrānumeyasāmānyena liṅgasāmānyasyānuvidhānadarśanaṃ sādharmyanidarśanam | tadyathā yat kriyāvat tad dravyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā śara iti | anumeyaviparyaye ca liṅgasyābhāvadarśanaṃ vaidharmyanidarśanam | tadyathā yad adravyaṃ tat kriyāvan na bhavati yathā satteti || 116 ||
literal_en: The Nidarśana, Instance, is of two kinds—that which corroborates by similarity or affirmation, and that which corroborates by dissimilarity or negation. The former kind consists in the recognition of the concomitance of the ‘indicative mark’ in general, with the ‘subject’ in general. E.g. (in the argument cited before) we have the statement—‘that which has action or motion has always been found to be a substance, as an arrow.’ The other kind of Instance consists in the recognition of the absence of the ‘indicative mark’ wherever there is absence of the ‘subject;’ e.g. (in the same argument) the statement—‘anything that is not a substance has no motion, as Being.’

ml_draft.text: നിദർശനം ദ്വിവിധം — സാധർമ്മ്യേണയും വൈധർമ്മ്യേണയും. അനുമേയസാമാന്യത്തോട് ലിംഗസാമാന്യത്തിന്റെ അനുവിധാനദർശനമാണു സാധർമ്മ്യനിദർശനം. ഉദാ: 'ക്രിയാവത്തായതെന്തോ അതെല്ലാം ദ്രവ്യമായി കാണപ്പെട്ടിരിക്കുന്നു — അമ്പ് പോലെ.' അനുമേയത്തിന്റെ വിപര്യയത്തിൽ ലിംഗത്തിന്റെ അഭാവദർശനമാണു വൈധർമ്മ്യനിദർശനം. ഉദാ: 'അദ്രവ്യമായതെന്തോ അത് ക്രിയാവത്താകുന്നില്ല — സത്ത പോലെ.'

en_simple_draft.text: *Nidarśana* (instance) is twofold: by *sādharmya* (similarity / affirmation) and by *vaidharmya* (dissimilarity / negation). *Sādharmyanidarśana* consists in the perception of the *liṅgasāmānya* (generic indicative) following upon the *anumeyasāmānya* (generic *anumeya*). E.g. (in the same argument): 'whatever has *kriyā* has been seen to be a *dravya* — like the arrow.' *Vaidharmyanidarśana* consists in the perception of the absence of the *liṅga* in the contrary of the *anumeya*. E.g.: 'whatever is *adravya* (non-substance) has no *kriyā* — like *sattā* (Being).'

sa_devanagari: अनेन निदर्शनाभासा निरस्ता भवन्ति । तद्यथा नित्यः शब्दोऽमूरत्वात् यद् अमूर्तं दृष्टं तन् नित्यं यथा परमाणुर्यथा कर्म यथा स्थाली यथा तमः अम्बरवद् इति यद् द्रव्यं तत् क्रियावद् दृष्टम् इति च लिङ्गानुमेयोभयाश्रयासिद्धाननुगतविपरीतानुगताः साधर्म्यनिदर्शनाभासाः । यद् अनित्यं तन् मूरतं दृष्टं यथा कर्म यथा परमाणुर्यथाकाशं यथा तमः घटवत् यन् निष्क्रियं तद् अद्रव्यञ्चेति लिङ्गानुमेयोभयाव्यावृत्ताश्रयासिद्धाव्यावृत्तविपरीतव्यावृत्ता वैधर्म्यनिदर्शनाभासा इति ॥ ११७ ॥
sa_iast: anena nidarśanābhāsā nirastā bhavanti | tadyathā nityaḥ śabdo'mūratvāt yad amūrtaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tan nityaṃ yathā paramāṇuryathā karma yathā sthālī yathā tamaḥ ambaravad iti yad dravyaṃ tat kriyāvad dṛṣṭam iti ca liṅgānumeyobhayāśrayāsiddhānanugataviparītānugatāḥ sādharmyanidarśanābhāsāḥ | yad anityaṃ tan mūrataṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā karma yathā paramāṇuryathākāśaṃ yathā tamaḥ ghaṭavat yan niṣkriyaṃ tad adravyañceti liṅgānumeyobhayāvyāvṛttāśrayāsiddhāvyāvṛttaviparītavyāvṛttā vaidharmyanidarśanābhāsā iti || 117 ||
literal_en: The above definition of ‘Instance’ sets; aside all false or wrong Instances. For instance, we have the argument—‘Sound is eternal, because it is immaterial’; and in corroboration of this we meet with the ‘Instance’—‘whatever is found to be immaterial is also eternal’,—e.g., (1) the Atom, (2) Action, (3) the Dish, (4) Darkness, (5) like ‘Ākāśa,’ and (6) ‘that which is a substance has always been found to have action or mobility.’ Here we have examples respectively of the six kinds of the ‘false Instance by affirmation:’ viz. (1) the ‘unknown indicative’ (2) the ‘unknown subject’ (3) ‘unknown indicative and subject’ (4) not applying to its own substratum, (5) the unconnected or incoherent, and (6) connected with the contrary.’ Similarly we have—‘that is which is noneternal is material,’—as (1) action,(2) atom (3) ‘like ākāśa,’ (4) darkness, (5) like the jar, (6) ‘that which is immobile is not a substance’—as examples respectively of the six kinds of the ‘false instance by negation by contraries’: viz.: (1) not excluded from the ‘indicative’ (2) not excluded from the ‘subject’ (3) not precluded from both, (4) not applying to its own substratum, (5) Non-preclusive and (5) Precluded from the contrary.

ml_draft.text: ഇതുകൊണ്ട് നിദർശനാഭാസങ്ങൾ നിരസ്തമാകുന്നു. ഉദാ: 'ശബ്ദം നിത്യം, അമൂർത്തത്വാത്; അമൂർത്തമായതെന്തോ അത് നിത്യമായി കാണപ്പെട്ടു — പരമാണു പോലെ, കർമ്മം പോലെ, സ്ഥാലി പോലെ, തമസ്സ് പോലെ, അംബരം പോലെ; യദ് ദ്രവ്യം തദ് ക്രിയാവദ് ദൃഷ്ടം' — ഇവ ലിംഗ-അനുമേയ-ഉഭയാശ്രയാസിദ്ധം, അനനുഗതം, വിപരീതാനുഗതം എന്നിങ്ങനെയുള്ള സാധർമ്മ്യനിദർശനാഭാസങ്ങൾ. 'യദനിത്യം തദ്മൂർത്തം ദൃഷ്ടം — കർമ്മം പോലെ, പരമാണു പോലെ, ആകാശം പോലെ, തമസ്സ് പോലെ, ഘടം പോലെ; യദ് നിഷ്ക്രിയം തദ് അദ്രവ്യം ച' — ഇവ ലിംഗ-അനുമേയ-ഉഭയാവ്യാവൃത്താശ്രയാസിദ്ധം, അവ്യാവൃത്തം, വിപരീതവ്യാവൃത്തം എന്നിങ്ങനെയുള്ള വൈധർമ്മ്യനിദർശനാഭാസങ്ങൾ.

en_simple_draft.text: By this definition, all *nidarśanābhāsa*s (false instances) are excluded. For example, the argument 'sound is *nitya* (eternal), because it is *amūrta* (immaterial); whatever is *amūrta* has been seen to be *nitya* — as the *paramāṇu*, as *karma*, as the dish, as *tamas* (darkness), as *ākāśa*; and 'whatever is *dravya* has been seen to have *kriyā*' — these illustrate the six false *sādharmya-nidarśana*s: (1) *liṅgāśrayāsiddha* (the *liṅga*'s substrate unknown), (2) *anumeyāśrayāsiddha* (the *anumeya*'s substrate unknown), (3) *ubhayāśrayāsiddha* (both unknown), (4) not applying to its own substrate, (5) *ananugata* (unconnected), and (6) *viparītānugata* (connected with the contrary). Likewise: 'whatever is *anitya* is *mūrta* — as *karma*, as *paramāṇu*, as *ākāśa*, as *tamas*, as the jar; and what is *niṣkriya* (without action) is also *adravya*' — these illustrate the corresponding false *vaidharmya-nidarśana*s: (1) *liṅga*-non-excluded, (2) *anumeya*-non-excluded, (3) both non-excluded, (4) not applying to its own substrate, (5) *avyāvṛtta* (non-preclusive), and (6) precluded from the contrary.

sa_devanagari: निदर्शनेऽनुमेयसामान्येन सह दृष्टस्य्स लिङ्गसामान्यस्यानुमेयेऽन्वानयनम् अनुसन्धानम् । अनुमेयधर्मात्रत्वेनाभितं लिङ्गसामान्यम् अनुपलब्धशक्तिकं निदर्शने साध्यधर्मसामान्येन सह दृष्टम् अनुमेये येन वचनेनानुसन्धीयते तदनुसन्धानम् । तथा च वायुः क्रियावान् इति । अनुमेयाभावे च तस्यासत्त्वम् उपलभ्य न च तथा वायुर्निष्क्रिय इति ॥ ११८ ॥
sa_iast: nidarśane'numeyasāmānyena saha dṛṣṭasysa liṅgasāmānyasyānumeye'nvānayanam anusandhānam | anumeyadharmātratvenābhitaṃ liṅgasāmānyam anupalabdhaśaktikaṃ nidarśane sādhyadharmasāmānyena saha dṛṣṭam anumeye yena vacanenānusandhīyate tadanusandhānam | tathā ca vāyuḥ kriyāvān iti | anumeyābhāve ca tasyāsattvam upalabhya na ca tathā vāyurniṣkriya iti || 118 ||
literal_en: The reiteration, of the concomitance of theft ‘Indicative’ in general with the ‘Subject,’ after the former has been perceived, in the ‘Instance,’ along with the ‘Subject’ in general,—constituted the Ānusandhāna [Anusandhāna?]. That is to say, the ‘Indicative’ in general is put forward (in the, Premiss)^ as a qualification of the ‘Subject,’ and not as having any potencies; and in the ‘Instance,’ it is pointed out as perceived along with the qualification of the Sādhya ‘(object of Inference) in general; and the statement that reiterates fact of its existence in the ‘Subject,’ is what is called the ‘Anūsandhāna’ (the Minor Premise.) E.g., in the same argument, the statement that ‘Air is mobile’; and also the statement that ‘the Air is not immobile’ which follows from the recognition of the fact of the ‘indicative’ not being concomitant with the absence of the ‘subject’.

ml_draft.text: നിദർശനത്തിൽ അനുമേയസാമാന്യത്തോടു കൂടി ദൃഷ്ടമായ ലിംഗസാമാന്യത്തെ അനുമേയത്തിലേക്ക് അന്വാനയനം ചെയ്യുന്നതാണു അനുസന്ധാനം. അനുമേയധർമ്മത്തിന്റെ വിശേഷണത്വേന അഭിഹിതമായ ലിംഗസാമാന്യം — അനുപലബ്ധശക്തികമായി — നിദർശനത്തിൽ സാധ്യധർമ്മസാമാന്യത്തോടു കൂടി ദൃഷ്ടമാകുമ്പോൾ, അനുമേയത്തിൽ ഏതു വചനം കൊണ്ട് അനുസന്ധിക്കുന്നുവോ — അതാണു അനുസന്ധാനം. ഉദാ: 'വായു ക്രിയാവാൻ' എന്നതും — അനുമേയത്തിന്റെ അഭാവത്തിൽ അതിന്റെ അസത്ത്വം ഉപലബ്ധിച്ച്, 'വായു അക്രിയയല്ല' എന്നതും.

en_simple_draft.text: *Anusandhāna* is the bringing-down (*anvānayana*) into the *anumeya* of the *liṅgasāmānya* (generic indicative) which has been seen, in the *nidarśana*, together with the *anumeyasāmānya* (generic *anumeya*). The *liṅgasāmānya* — first uttered as a mere qualification of the *anumeyadharma*, with no demonstrated power — is then perceived in the *nidarśana* together with the generic *sādhya-dharma*; and the statement that reasserts its presence in the *anumeya* is *anusandhāna*. E.g. (in the same argument), 'wind possesses *kriyā*'; and likewise, having recognised the absence of the *liṅga* in the absence of the *anumeya*, the statement 'wind is not *niṣkriya*.'

sa_devanagari: अनुमेयत्वेनोद्दिष्टे चानिश्चिते च परेषां निश्चयापादनार्थं प्रतिज्ञायाः पुनर्वचनं प्रप्त्याम्नायः । प्रतिपाद्यत्वेनोद्दिष्टे चानिश्चिते च परेषां हेत्वादिभिरवयवैराहितशक्तीनां परिसमाप्तेन वाक्येन निश्चयापादनार्थं प्रतिज्ञायाः पुनर्वचनं प्रत्यामनायः । तस्माद् द्रव्यम् एवेति  । न ह्येतस्मिन् न सति परेषाम् अवयवानां समस्तानां व्यस्तानां वा तदर्थवाचकत्वम् अस्ति गम्यमानार्थत्वाद् इति चेन् न अतिप्रसङ्गात् । तथाहि प्रतिज्ञानन्तरं हेतुमात्राभिधानं कर्तव्यं विदुषामन्वयव्यतिरेकस्मरणात् तदर्थावगतिर्भविष्यतीति तस्माद् अत्रैवार्थपरिसमाप्तिः । कथम् अनित्यः शब्द इत्यनेनानिश्चितानित्यत्वमात्रविशिष्टः शब्दः कथ्यते प्रयत्नानन्तरीयकत्वाद् इत्यनेनानित्यत्वसाधनधर्ममात्रम् अभिधीयते । इह यत् प्रयत्नानन्तरीयकं तदनित्यं दृष्टं यथा घट इत्यनेन साध्यसामान्येन साधनसामान्यस्यानुगाममात्रम् उच्यते । नित्यम् अप्रयत्नानन्तरीयकं दृष्टं यथाकाशम् इत्यनेन साध्याभावेन साधनस्यासत्त्वं प्रदर्श्यते । तथा च प्रयत्नानन्तरीयकः शब्दो दृष्टो न च तथाकाशवद् अप्रयत्नानन्तरीयकः शब्द इत्यन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यां दृष्टसामर्थ्यस्य साधनसामान्यस्य शब्देऽनुसन्धानं गम्यते तस्माद् अनित्यः शब्द त्यनेनानित्य एव शब्द इति प्रतिपिपादयिषितार्थपरिसमाप्तिर्गम्यते तस्मात् पञ्चावयवेनैव वाक्येन परेषां स्वनिश्चितार्थप्र्तिपादनं क्रियते इत्येतत् परार्थानुमानं सिद्धम् इति ॥ ११९ ॥
sa_iast: anumeyatvenoddiṣṭe cāniścite ca pareṣāṃ niścayāpādanārthaṃ pratijñāyāḥ punarvacanaṃ praptyāmnāyaḥ | pratipādyatvenoddiṣṭe cāniścite ca pareṣāṃ hetvādibhiravayavairāhitaśaktīnāṃ parisamāptena vākyena niścayāpādanārthaṃ pratijñāyāḥ punarvacanaṃ pratyāmanāyaḥ | tasmād dravyam eveti | na hyetasmin na sati pareṣām avayavānāṃ samastānāṃ vyastānāṃ vā tadarthavācakatvam asti gamyamānārthatvād iti cen na atiprasaṅgāt | tathāhi pratijñānantaraṃ hetumātrābhidhānaṃ kartavyaṃ viduṣāmanvayavyatirekasmaraṇāt tadarthāvagatirbhaviṣyatīti tasmād atraivārthaparisamāptiḥ | katham anityaḥ śabda ityanenāniścitānityatvamātraviśiṣṭaḥ śabdaḥ kathyate prayatnānantarīyakatvād ityanenānityatvasādhanadharmamātram abhidhīyate | iha yat prayatnānantarīyakaṃ tadanityaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā ghaṭa ityanena sādhyasāmānyena sādhanasāmānyasyānugāmamātram ucyate | nityam aprayatnānantarīyakaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathākāśam ityanena sādhyābhāvena sādhanasyāsattvaṃ pradarśyate | tathā ca prayatnānantarīyakaḥ śabdo dṛṣṭo na ca tathākāśavad aprayatnānantarīyakaḥ śabda ityanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ dṛṣṭasāmarthyasya sādhanasāmānyasya śabde'nusandhānaṃ gamyate tasmād anityaḥ śabda tyanenānitya eva śabda iti pratipipādayiṣitārthaparisamāptirgamyate tasmāt pañcāvayavenaiva vākyena pareṣāṃ svaniścitārthaprtipādanaṃ kriyate ityetat parārthānumānaṃ siddham iti || 119 ||
literal_en:
The ‘subject’ having been mentioned as the object of Inference, and yet not being fully ascertained as such, we have a reiteration of the Conclusion (Pratijñā) for the purpose of bringing about certainty in the mind of the other person; and this Reiteration is called the ‘Pratyāmnāya.’ That is to say, something is at first pointed out as to be proved; and when it is not known quite for a certainty to be such as is wanted to be proved, then—for the sake of such persons as have acquired the faculty of recognising the truth, by means of the ‘Reason’ and other aforesaid ‘Factors’ of the syllogism,—we have a reiteration of the conclusion; and this is what is called the ‘Pratyāmnāya.’ E.g. (in the same argument) the statement ‘therefore Air is a substance.’

As long as this reassertion is not made, none of the other ‘Factors’ either individually or collectively has the power to express what is meant to be expressed by it.

Objection: “But what is expressed by it may certainly be implied by the other members.”

Reply: No so; as if it were so, then we would have many undesirable irregularities. As, (if we were to depend upon implications), then after stating the conclusion (in the Pratijñā) it would be necessary to assert the ‘Reason’ only; as the learned are sure to remember the necessary ‘invariable concomitance’ {sought to be put forward in the ‘Instance’), and thence to deduce the necessary premisses and conclusions.

For these reasons the argument must be regarded as ending with the ‘Pratyāmnāya’ (or ‘Nigamana’).

Question: ‘How so?’

Answer: For instance, in the first place we have the ‘statement of the conclusion' in the form—‘Sound is evanescent,’—wherein we have only ‘sound’ mentioned as having the uncertain qualification of ‘evanescence’; secondly we have the statement of the ‘Reason’ in the form—‘because it always follows from effort,’—wherein we have the mere mention of a property calculated to prove the ‘evanescence’; thirdly we have the ‘statement of the Instance’ in the form—‘in the world all that is found to follow from effort is also found to be evanescent, as the jar’—wherein we have merely the mention of the concomitance of the ‘Reason’ (‘following from effort’) with the ‘Object of Inference’ (‘evanescence’) in general; and similarly we may have the ‘statement of the negative Instance’ in the form—‘the eternal is never found to follow from any effort, as the Ākāça,’—wherein is pointed out the absence of the ‘Reason’ in the absence of the ‘object’; fourthly we have the statement of the ‘Anusandhāna’ in the two forms of affirmation and negation—‘sound is found to follow from effort’ and ‘sound is not found like Ākāśa to be independent of effort,’—wherein we have the reiteration of the ‘Reason’ in general, whose powers have been ascertained by means of affirmation and negation, in ‘sound’; and then alone fifthly and lastly have we the certain conclusion (the Pratyāmnāya’) in the form—‘therefore sound must be evanescent.’ And thus we find that it is only in this way that we find the last ‘member’ affording the desired final conclusion; and hence we find that it is only by means of the ‘five-membered’ argament that something known for certain by the speaker can be proved to another person.

Such then, is the Inference ‘for the sake of others.’—(IX-i-1, 2.)

ml_draft.text: അനുമേയത്വേന ഉദ്ദിഷ്ടവും അനിശ്ചിതവുമായതിൽ പരർക്ക് നിശ്ചയം ആപാദിക്കാൻ വേണ്ടി പ്രതിജ്ഞയുടെ പുനർവചനമാണു പ്രത്യാമ്നായം. പ്രതിപാദ്യത്വേന ഉദ്ദിഷ്ടവും അനിശ്ചിതവുമായ പരർക്ക് — ഹേതു മുതലായ അവയവങ്ങളാൽ ആഹിതശക്തികൾ ആകുന്നവർക്ക് — പരിസമാപ്തമായ വാക്യത്താൽ നിശ്ചയം ആപാദിക്കാൻ വേണ്ടി പ്രതിജ്ഞയുടെ പുനർവചനമാണു പ്രത്യാമ്നായം. ഉദാ: 'അതിനാൽ ദ്രവ്യം തന്നെ' (എന്നത്). ഇത് ഇല്ലെങ്കിൽ ശേഷം അവയവങ്ങൾ — സമസ്തമോ വ്യസ്തമോ — ആ അർത്ഥത്തെ വാചകമാക്കാൻ ശക്തി ഇല്ല. 'അർത്ഥം ഗമ്യമാനമാണല്ലോ' എന്നു പറഞ്ഞാൽ — അല്ല, അതിപ്രസംഗം ഉണ്ടാകും. അതായത് — പ്രതിജ്ഞാനന്തരം ഹേതുമാത്രാഭിധാനം ചെയ്താൽ മതി, വിദ്വാന്മാർ അന്വയ-വ്യതിരേകം സ്മരിച്ച് അർത്ഥം അവഗതമാക്കും — അപ്രകാരമെങ്കിൽ അവിടെത്തന്നെ അർത്ഥപരിസമാപ്തി. എങ്ങനെ? 'ശബ്ദം അനിത്യം' എന്നതുകൊണ്ട് അനിശ്ചിതാനിത്യത്വവിശിഷ്ടനായ ശബ്ദം മാത്രം പറയപ്പെടുന്നു; 'പ്രയത്നാനന്തരീയകത്വാത്' എന്നതുകൊണ്ട് അനിത്യത്വസാധനധർമ്മമാത്രം അഭിധീയിക്കപ്പെടുന്നു. 'ഇഹ യത് പ്രയത്നാനന്തരീയകം തദനിത്യം ദൃഷ്ടം — ഘടം പോലെ' എന്നതുകൊണ്ട് സാധ്യസാമാന്യത്തോട് സാധനസാമാന്യത്തിന്റെ അനുഗാമമാത്രം. 'നിത്യം അപ്രയത്നാനന്തരീയകം ദൃഷ്ടം — ആകാശം പോലെ' എന്നതുകൊണ്ട് സാധ്യാഭാവത്തിൽ സാധനത്തിന്റെ അസത്ത്വം പ്രദർശിതം. 'അപ്രകാരം പ്രയത്നാനന്തരീയകൻ ശബ്ദം ദൃഷ്ടം; ആകാശം പോലെ ശബ്ദം അപ്രയത്നാനന്തരീയകനല്ല' — ഈ അന്വയ-വ്യതിരേകങ്ങളാൽ ദൃഷ്ടസാമർത്ഥ്യമായ സാധനസാമാന്യത്തെ ശബ്ദത്തിൽ അനുസന്ധിക്കുന്നതായി ഗമ്യമാകുന്നു. അതിനാൽ 'അനിത്യഃ ശബ്ദഃ' എന്നതുകൊണ്ട് — 'ശബ്ദം അനിത്യം തന്നെ' — എന്നു പ്രതിപാദിക്കാൻ ആഗ്രഹിച്ച അർത്ഥപരിസമാപ്തി ഗമ്യമാകുന്നു. അതിനാൽ പഞ്ചാവയവവാക്യത്താൽത്തന്നെ പരർക്ക് സ്വനിശ്ചിതാർത്ഥപ്രതിപാദനം ചെയ്യപ്പെടുന്നു — ഇതാണു പരാർത്ഥാനുമാനം എന്നു സിദ്ധം.

en_simple_draft.text: When something has been mentioned as the *anumeya* but is not yet ascertained, the *punarvacana* (re-statement) of the *pratijñā* — for the purpose of producing certainty in others — is *pratyāmnāya*. For others to whom (the matter) has been put forward as *pratipādya* (to be conveyed) but not ascertained, and in whom the *avayava*s (members) such as *hetu* etc. have already deposited their force, — the re-statement of the *pratijñā* in a complete sentence, in order to bring about certainty, is *pratyāmnāya*. E.g. 'therefore (wind) is a *dravya*.' Without this (re-statement), none of the other members, taken individually or collectively, has the power to express what is meant. If one objects 'but the meaning is implied,' — no, for that would lead to over-extension (*atiprasaṅga*). For instance, after the *pratijñā*, only the bare *hetu* would suffice — since the learned, recalling *anvaya* and *vyatireka*, would arrive at the meaning; in which case the meaning would be exhausted right there. How is this not so? In 'sound is *anitya*' only sound qualified by an unascertained *anitya-tva* is mentioned; in 'because it follows upon *prayatna* (effort)' only the property serving to prove *anitya-tva* is stated; in 'whatever follows upon *prayatna* has been seen to be *anitya*, as the jar' only the concomitance of the generic *sādhana* with the generic *sādhya* is stated; in 'the *nitya* has been seen as not following upon *prayatna*, as *ākāśa*' is shown the absence of the *sādhana* in the absence of the *sādhya*; and in 'thus sound has been seen to follow upon *prayatna*, and like *ākāśa* sound is not non-following-upon-*prayatna*' is conveyed the *anusandhāna* in sound of the generic *sādhana* whose power has been demonstrated by *anvaya* and *vyatireka*. Therefore, by 'sound is *anitya*' it is conveyed that the *artha* meant — 'sound is just *anitya*' — has been completed. Hence it is established that *parārthānumāna* is the conveying to others of one's own ascertained meaning by means of the five-membered sentence.

sa_devanagari: विशेषदर्शनजम् अवधारणज्ञानं संशयविरोधी निर्णयः । एतद् एव प्रत्यक्षम् अनुमानं वा । यद् विशेषदर्शनात् संशयविरोध्युत्पद्यते स प्रत्यक्षनिर्णयः । यथा स्थाणुपुरुषयोरूर्ध्वतामात्रसादृश्यालोचनाद् विशेषेष्वप्रत्यक्षेषूभयविशेषानुस्मरणात् किम् अयं स्थाणुपुरुषो वेति संशयोत्पत्तौ शिरह्पाण्यादिदर्शनात् पुरुष एवायम् इत्यवधारणज्ञानं प्रत्यक्षनिर्णयः । विषाणमात्रदर्शनाद् गौर्गवयो वेति संशयोत्पत्तौ सास्नामात्रदर्शनाद् गौरु एवायम् इत्यवधारणज्ञानम् अनुमाननिर्णय इति ॥ १२० ॥
sa_iast: viśeṣadarśanajam avadhāraṇajñānaṃ saṃśayavirodhī nirṇayaḥ | etad eva pratyakṣam anumānaṃ vā | yad viśeṣadarśanāt saṃśayavirodhyutpadyate sa pratyakṣanirṇayaḥ | yathā sthāṇupuruṣayorūrdhvatāmātrasādṛśyālocanād viśeṣeṣvapratyakṣeṣūbhayaviśeṣānusmaraṇāt kim ayaṃ sthāṇupuruṣo veti saṃśayotpattau śirahpāṇyādidarśanāt puruṣa evāyam ityavadhāraṇajñānaṃ pratyakṣanirṇayaḥ | viṣāṇamātradarśanād gaurgavayo veti saṃśayotpattau sāsnāmātradarśanād gauru evāyam ityavadhāraṇajñānam anumānanirṇaya iti || 121 ||
literal_en: A definite cognition brought about by the due perception of the special features, is called ‘Nirṇaya;’ and this is opposed to Doubtful Cognition. It is only this definite cognition that can be either ‘perceptive’ of ‘inferential.’ That which is produced by a sensuous perception of the special features, and sets aside all doubts, is the ‘perceptive judgment;’ e.g when we see a certain object standing before us, we may perceive only the tallness, which is a property common between the pole and the man, and not perceive any of the features belonging specifically to either; and then recalling to our mind the (other) features common to both, we have the doubtful cognition, as to whether the object before us is a pole of a. nan; after a time, perceiving that the object has a head and hands &c., we come to the definite cognition that it is a ‘man,’ and this is a case of the ‘perceptive Definite Cognition. Then again, seeing only a pair of horns in a thicket (and not any other parts of the animal’s body), we have the doubtful cognition that it is a cow or a Gavaya; and then noticing the presence of the dewlap, we have the Definite Cognition that it is a ‘cow and this is a case of the ‘inferential Definite Cognition.’—(IX-ii-12; X-i-3.)

ml_draft.text: വിശേഷദർശനത്തിൽ നിന്ന് ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്നതും, സംശയത്തിന്റെ വിരോധിയും ആയ അവധാരണജ്ഞാനമാണു നിർണയം. ഇത് പ്രത്യക്ഷമോ അനുമാനമോ ആകാം. വിശേഷദർശനത്തിൽ നിന്ന് സംശയവിരോധി ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്നതാണു പ്രത്യക്ഷനിർണയം. ഉദാ: സ്ഥാണുവിന്റെയും പുരുഷന്റെയും ഊർധ്വതാമാത്രം ആലോചിച്ച്, വിശേഷങ്ങൾ അപ്രത്യക്ഷമായിരിക്കുമ്പോൾ — ഉഭയത്തിന്റെയും വിശേഷങ്ങൾ അനുസ്മരിച്ച്, 'ഇത് സ്ഥാണുവോ പുരുഷനോ' എന്ന സംശയം ഉത്ഭവിക്കുമ്പോൾ; ശിരസ്സ്, പാണി മുതലായവ കണ്ടാൽ 'ഇത് പുരുഷൻ തന്നെ' എന്ന അവധാരണജ്ഞാനമാണു പ്രത്യക്ഷനിർണയം. വിഷാണമാത്രം കണ്ട് 'ഇത് ഗോവോ ഗവയമോ' എന്ന സംശയം ഉത്ഭവിക്കുമ്പോൾ; സാസ്നമാത്രം കണ്ടാൽ 'ഇത് ഗോവ് തന്നെ' എന്ന അവധാരണജ്ഞാനമാണു അനുമാനനിർണയം.

en_simple_draft.text: *Nirṇaya* — definite cognition — is the *avadhāraṇa-jñāna* (ascertaining cognition) born of *viśeṣa-darśana* (perception of distinguishing features), and is the opposite of *saṃśaya* (doubt). *Nirṇaya* may be either *pratyakṣa* or *anumāna*. That which arises from *viśeṣa-darśana* through *pratyakṣa* and overcomes doubt is *pratyakṣa-nirṇaya*. E.g.: when one perceives only the bare uprightness common to a *sthāṇu* (post) and a *puruṣa* (man), and the distinguishing features of neither are perceived, recalling features common to both, the doubt 'is this a *sthāṇu* or a *puruṣa*?' arises; subsequently, perceiving head, hands, etc., the *avadhāraṇa-jñāna* 'this is a *puruṣa*' is *pratyakṣa-nirṇaya*. Again, perceiving only the bare horns (in a thicket), the doubt 'is this a cow or a *gavaya*?' arises; perceiving the *sāsna* (dewlap), the *avadhāraṇa-jñāna* 'this is a cow' is *anumāna-nirṇaya*.

sa_devanagari: लिङ्गदर्शनेच्छानुस्मरणाद्यपेक्षाद् आत्ममनसोः सम्योगविशेषात् पट्वाभ्यासादरप्रत्ययजनिताच्च संस्काराद् दृष्टश्रुतानुभूतेष्वर्थेषु शेषानुव्यवसायेच्छानुस्मरणद्वेषहेतुरतीतविषया स्मृतिरिति ॥ १२१ ॥
sa_iast: liṅgadarśanecchānusmaraṇādyapekṣād ātmamanasoḥ samyogaviśeṣāt paṭvābhyāsādarapratyayajanitācca saṃskārād dṛṣṭaśrutānubhūteṣvartheṣu śeṣānuvyavasāyecchānusmaraṇadveṣaheturatītaviṣayā smṛtiriti || 121 ||
literal_en: From the contact of the soul and the mind as aided by such causes as the perception of an ‘Indicative,’ ‘desire’ (for remembering) and ‘associated ideas,’ and the like, and from a faculty produced by distinct cognition, by repetition and by an impressive regard (for the object concerned),—there arises a remembrance of objects seen, heard or experienced (inferred) in the past, which becomes the cause of the recalling of what remains (of a previous cognition), of desire, of associated or secondary remembrance, and of aversion.

ml_draft.text: ലിംഗദർശനം, ഇച്ഛ, അനുസ്മരണം മുതലായവയെ അപേക്ഷിച്ച് ഉണ്ടാകുന്ന ആത്മാവിന്റെയും മനസ്സിന്റെയും വിശിഷ്ടസംയോഗത്തിൽ നിന്നും — പട്വാഭ്യാസവും ആദരപ്രത്യയവും ജനിതമായ സംസ്കാരത്തിൽ നിന്നും — ദൃഷ്ടം, ശ്രുതം, അനുഭൂതം എന്നീ വസ്തുക്കളിൽ, ശേഷാനുവ്യവസായം, ഇച്ഛ, അനുസ്മരണം, ദ്വേഷം എന്നിവയുടെ ഹേതുവായി, അതീതവിഷയത്തിൽ ഉണ്ടാകുന്ന ജ്ഞാനമാണു സ്മൃതി.

en_simple_draft.text: From the *saṃyoga-viśeṣa* (special conjunction) of *ātman* and *manas* — aided by such causes as the perception of a *liṅga*, *icchā* (desire to remember) and *anusmaraṇa* (associated recollection) — and from the *saṃskāra* (impression) generated by clear practice (*paṭu-abhyāsa*) and attentive cognition (*ādara-pratyaya*), there arises, with respect to objects seen, heard or experienced (in the past), a cognition whose object is the past — being the cause of subsequent *anuvyavasāya*, *icchā*, *anusmaraṇa* and *dveṣa*. This is *smṛti*.

sa_devanagari: आम्नायविधात्qणाम् ऋषीणाम् अतीतानागतवर्तमानेष्वतीन्द्रियेष्वर्थेषु धर्मादिषु ग्रन्थोपनिबद्धेष्वनुपनिबद्धेषु चात्ममनसोः सम्योगाद् धर्मविशेषाच्च यत् प्रातिभं यथार्थनिवेदनं ज्ञानम् उत्पद्यते तदार्षम् इत्याचक्षते । तत् तु प्रस्तारेण देवर्षीणां कदाचिद् एव लौकिकानां यथा कन्यका ब्रवीति श्वो मे भाताऽऽगन्ति हृदयं मे कथयतीति ॥ १२२ ॥
sa_iast: āmnāyavidhātqṇām ṛṣīṇām atītānāgatavartamāneṣvatīndriyeṣvartheṣu dharmādiṣu granthopanibaddheṣvanupanibaddheṣu cātmamanasoḥ samyogād dharmaviśeṣācca yat prātibhaṃ yathārthanivedanaṃ jñānam utpadyate tadārṣam ityācakṣate | tat tu prastāreṇa devarṣīṇāṃ kadācid eva laukikānāṃ yathā kanyakā bravīti śvo me bhātā''ganti hṛdayaṃ me kathayatīti || 122 ||
literal_en:
In the case of the sages whose acts are in full accordance with the Vedas, we find that from the contact, of the Soul and the mind, as aided by a peculiar virtue, there appears an intuitional cognition true in all its objective details,—with regard to objects past, present and future, as also to Dharma and other (supersensuous) objects, such as are spoken of in the scriptures, as well as those that are not so mentioned; and this intuitional cognition is called ‘Ārṣa’ or ‘sagic.’

This cognition as a rule belongs to the Divine Sages; and only in. rare instances to human beings also; as when we find a little girl saying ‘my heart tells me that my brother will come tomorrow.’

ml_draft.text: ആമ്നായത്തിന്റെ വിധാതാക്കളായ ഋഷിമാർക്ക് — അതീത-അനാഗത-വർത്തമാന വസ്തുക്കളിൽ, അതീന്ദ്രിയങ്ങളായ ധർമ്മാദി വിഷയങ്ങളിൽ, ഗ്രന്ഥോപനിബദ്ധങ്ങളിലും അനുപനിബദ്ധങ്ങളിലും — ആത്മാവിന്റെയും മനസ്സിന്റെയും സംയോഗത്തിൽ നിന്നും ധർമ്മവിശേഷത്തിൽ നിന്നും, യഥാർത്ഥനിവേദനം ചെയ്യുന്ന പ്രാതിഭമായ ജ്ഞാനം ഉത്ഭവിക്കുന്നു. അതാണു 'ആർഷ'ം എന്നു പറയപ്പെടുന്നത്. ഇത് സാധാരണയായി ദേവർഷിമാർക്ക്; ലൗകികർക്കു ചിലപ്പോൾ മാത്രം. ഉദാ: ഒരു കന്യക 'നാളെ എന്റെ സഹോദരൻ വരും; എന്റെ ഹൃദയം പറയുന്നു' എന്നു പറയുമ്പോൾ.

en_simple_draft.text: In the case of the *ṛṣi*s — the *āmnāya-vidhātṛ*s (framers of the Veda) — from the *saṃyoga* of *ātman* and *manas* aided by a special *dharma*, there arises a *prātibha* (intuitive) *jñāna* that conveys reality as it is — concerning past, future and present things, concerning *atīndriya* (supersensuous) objects such as *dharma* etc., whether recorded in scriptural texts or not. This is what is called *ārṣa* (sagic) cognition. It belongs as a rule to the *devarṣi*s; only occasionally to ordinary persons — as when a young girl says 'tomorrow my brother will come; my heart tells me so.'
